You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

nt in a

terial uncured breach exceeding 60 days, and cessation of product support; and

k while preserving TechNova's ownership position in brackets as an alternativ=

n for TechNova. We are integrating MeridianIQ outputs directly into a consume=
r-facing lending platform, and the risk allocation on downstream third-party =
claims needs to be addressed squarely in the agreement.

mnity coverage, TechNova would need to revisit the overall risk allocation fr=

pril 21, 2025) as the base document, with Draft 2 tracked changes accepted to=

lean version. The markup will incorporate agreed positions, propose compromis=
e language on partially resolved items, and flag remaining open issues with a=
nnotations. We would ask that Meridian and Capstone Bridger turn comments pro=
mptly upon receipt to maintain the June 15 execution target.

4. De-identified data certification requirement

engagement from your side. It's important that we maintain this momentum =E2=
=80=94 the initial term commencement on July 1, 2025, and Go-Live on October =
1, 2025, don't leave us a lot of runway for extended back-and-forth on the re=
maining open items. Let's aim to close as much as we can in the next two week=
s.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS]{.underline}**
**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.
**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

99: **[ARTICLE 2 --- LICENSE GRANT AND SCOPE OF USE]{.underline}**
100: 
101: **Section 2.1 --- License Grant**
102: 
103: Subject to and conditioned upon Customer\'s compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including timely payment of all Fees, Vendor hereby grants to Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license during the Term to access and use the Platform solely for Customer\'s internal business operations in connection with Customer\'s lending technology product known as LendStream. The license granted hereunder includes the right to access and use the Platform through the APIs provided by Vendor, to submit Customer Data for processing through the Platform, and to receive and use the outputs generated by the Platform in connection with LendStream. This license is further conditioned on Customer\'s compliance with the Documentation and all applicable laws, rules, and regulations.
104: 
105: **Section 2.2 --- Scope of Authorized Use**
106: 
107: Customer may permit its employees, and authorized contractors who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in Article 7, to access and use the Platform on Customer\'s behalf and in furtherance of Customer\'s authorized use hereunder. Customer shall be responsible for all acts and omissions of its employees and authorized contractors in connection with their access to and use of the Platform. Use of the Platform is limited to the processing, analysis, and classification of Customer Data in support of LendStream\'s document processing workflows. Customer shall not use the Platform for any purpose other than as expressly authorized by this Agreement. Customer shall not exceed the Included API Calls in any Contract Year, except as subject to the overage charges set forth in Section 4.3.
108: 
109: **Section 2.3 --- Restrictions**
110: 
111: Customer acknowledges that the Platform and Base Model represent proprietary technology of Vendor. Customer shall not, and shall not permit any third party to:
112: 
113: > \(a\) reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise attempt to derive the source code, algorithms, data structures, or underlying ideas of the Platform or the Base Model, except to the extent that such restriction is expressly prohibited by applicable law notwithstanding a contractual prohibition;
114: >
115: > \(b\) sublicense, sell, resell, lease, rent, loan, distribute, or otherwise make available the Platform or any component thereof to any third party, whether as a service bureau, managed service, or otherwise;
116: >
117: > \(c\) use the Platform or any output thereof for competitive benchmarking, competitive analysis, or to develop, train, or improve a product or service that competes with the Platform or any of Vendor\'s other products or services;
118: >
119: > \(d\) remove, obscure, alter, or deface any proprietary notices, labels, or marks on or in the Platform, the Documentation, or any output thereof;
120: >
121: > \(e\) access the Platform other than through the APIs and access mechanisms provided by Vendor, including without limitation by scraping, crawling, or using any automated means not expressly authorized by Vendor;
122: >
123: > \(f\) attempt to extract, reconstruct, distill, or reverse engineer model weights, architectures, training data, or any other proprietary components from the Platform, whether through prompt injection, model inversion, membership inference, or any other technique; or
124: >
125: > \(g\) use the Platform in any manner that violates applicable law or regulation, or that infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates the Intellectual Property Rights or other rights of any third party.
126: 
127: **Section 2.4 --- Reservation of Rights**
128: 
129: Except for the limited license expressly granted in Section 2.1, Vendor reserves all rights in and to the Platform, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. No implied licenses are granted under this Agreement by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Customer\'s right to access and use the Platform is limited to the express license grant set forth in Section 2.1, and all other rights are expressly reserved by Vendor. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any right to access the source code or model weights of the Platform or the Base Model.
130: 
131: **[ARTICLE 3 --- IMPLEMENTATION AND TRAINING SERVICES]{.underline}**
132: 
133: **Section 3.1 --- Implementation Services**
134: 
135: Vendor shall perform the Implementation Services as described in the initial Statement of Work attached hereto as Exhibit A (the \"**Initial SOW**\") and any additional Statements of Work that may be executed by the Parties from time to time pursuant to this Article 3. The Implementation Services under the Initial SOW shall include, without limitation: (a) provisioning and configuration of Customer\'s dedicated Platform environment; (b) API integration of the Platform with Customer\'s LendStream product; (c) fine-tuning of the Base Model using Customer Data to optimize the Platform\'s performance for Customer\'s specific document processing requirements; (d) initial accuracy validation and testing of the fine-tuned model; and (e) initial training of Customer\'s designated personnel on the use and operation of the Platform. All Implementation Services shall be performed by Vendor personnel who are qualified and experienced in the relevant subject matter.
136: 
137: **Section 3.2 --- Implementation Milestones**
138: 
139: The Implementation Services shall be performed in accordance with the following milestones, as further described in Exhibit A:
140: 
141: > **Milestone 1 --- SOW Execution.** Execution of the Initial SOW by both Parties. Achievement of Milestone 1 shall trigger payment of the first installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(a).
142: >
143: > **Milestone 2 --- Go-Live.** Successful achievement of Go-Live, targeted for October 1, 2025, at which point the Platform shall be made available for production use by Customer. Achievement of Milestone 2 shall trigger payment of the second installment of the Implementation Fee as set forth in Section 4.2(b). Go-Live shall be conditioned upon the Platform performing materially in accordance with the Documentation, as mutually confirmed by the Parties through the acceptance process described in Exhibit A.
144: 
145: Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve the targeted Go-Live date, but the targeted Go-Live date is an estimate only and shall not constitute a guaranteed delivery date. Delays caused by Customer\'s failure to fulfill its cooperation obligations under Section 3.3 shall extend the targeted Go-Live date by a commensurate period.
146: 
147: **Section 3.3 --- Customer Cooperation**
148: 
149: Customer acknowledges that Vendor\'s ability to perform the Implementation Services is dependent upon Customer\'s timely cooperation and assistance. Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation in connection with the Implementation Services, including without limitation: (a) timely provision of Customer Data in the format and quality reasonably specified by Vendor; (b) access to Customer\'s systems and environments as reasonably necessary for Vendor to perform API integration and testing; (c) designation of qualified Customer personnel with appropriate subject matter expertise to serve as points of contact and to participate in the implementation process, including providing timely feedback and approvals; and (d) such other cooperation as may be reasonably requested by Vendor and described in the applicable Statement of Work. Customer\'s failure to provide timely cooperation may result in delays in the Implementation Services, and Vendor shall not be responsible for any such delays to the extent caused by Customer\'s failure to perform its cooperation obligations under this Section 3.3.
150: 
151: **Section 3.4 --- Change Orders**
152: 
153: Any changes to the scope, timeline, deliverables, or fees for Implementation Services shall be documented in a mutually agreed written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No change to the Implementation Services shall be binding unless set forth in a duly executed change order. Each change order shall specify the nature of the change, any impact on the project timeline and milestones, and any additional fees associated with the change. Vendor shall not be obligated to perform any work outside the scope of an executed Statement of Work or change order.
154: 
155: **[ARTICLE 4 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**
156: 
157: **Section 4.1 --- Annual Platform Fee**
158: 
159: In consideration of the license and access rights granted hereunder, Customer shall pay to Vendor an annual platform fee of Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,400,000) per Contract Year (the \"**Annual Platform Fee**\"). The Annual Platform Fee shall be invoiced by Vendor in equal monthly installments of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$200,000) per month, with each monthly invoice due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice. Vendor shall issue monthly invoices on or about the first business day of each calendar month during the Term, beginning with the first calendar month following the Effective Date.
160: 
161: **Section 4.2 --- Implementation Fee**
162: 
163: In consideration of the Implementation Services described in Article 3 and Exhibit A, Customer shall pay to Vendor a one-time implementation and fine-tuning fee of Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$850,000) (the \"**Implementation Fee**\"). The Implementation Fee shall be payable in two (2) equal installments of Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000) each, as follows:
164: 
165: > \(a\) **First Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following execution of the Initial SOW (Milestone 1).
166: >
167: > \(b\) **Second Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following achievement of Go-Live (Milestone 2).
168: 
169: **Section 4.3 --- Overage Fees**
170: 
171: The Annual Platform Fee includes forty million (40,000,000) API calls per Contract Year (the \"**Included API Calls**\"). API calls made by Customer in excess of the Included API Calls during any Contract Year shall be invoiced by Vendor at a rate of twelve-thousandths of a dollar (\$0.012) per API call (the \"**Overage Rate**\"). Overage Fees shall be invoiced monthly in arrears, based on Vendor\'s metering and usage data for the applicable calendar month. Each such invoice shall include a summary of API call usage for the month, including the number of API calls consumed and the number of remaining Included API Calls for the applicable Contract Year. Overage Fee invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.
172: 
173: **Section 4.4 --- Taxes**
174: 
175: All Fees set forth in this Agreement are exclusive of any and all applicable taxes, duties, levies, or similar governmental charges (collectively, \"**Taxes**\"). Customer shall be responsible for, and shall pay, all sales, use, value-added, goods and services, withholding, and similar Taxes imposed on or in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, excluding taxes based on Vendor\'s net income, capital, or franchise taxes assessed against Vendor. If Vendor is required by law to collect any Taxes from Customer, Vendor shall include such Taxes on the applicable invoice and Customer shall remit payment of such Taxes together with the applicable Fees. If Customer is required to withhold any Taxes from amounts payable to Vendor, Customer shall gross up the payment so that Vendor receives the full amount of the invoiced Fees after deduction of such withholding Taxes.
176: 
177: **Section 4.5 --- Late Payments**
178: 
179: Any undisputed Fees not paid when due shall accrue interest at the lesser of (a) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (18% per annum) or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received in full by Vendor. In addition, Vendor may, upon at least fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice to Customer, suspend Customer\'s access to the Platform if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than forty-five (45) days past its due date, and such suspension shall continue until all outstanding amounts, including accrued interest, have been paid in full. The foregoing remedies are in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other remedies available to Vendor under this Agreement or applicable law.
180: 
181: **Section 4.6 --- Total Contract Value**
182: 
183: For informational purposes and clarity, the total contract value for the Initial Term (exclusive of Overage Fees and Taxes) is as follows:
184: 
185: > \(a\) Annual Platform Fees for three (3) Contract Years: \$2,400,000 × 3 = **\$7,200,000**;
186: >
187: > \(b\) Implementation Fee (one-time): **\$850,000**;
188: >
189: > \(c\) **Total:** **\$8,050,000**.
190: 
191: The foregoing total contract value is an estimate for informational purposes only and does not include any Overage Fees, Taxes, or fees for additional Statements of Work that may be executed during the Term. The total contract value does not limit Vendor\'s right to invoice for Overage Fees or other amounts payable under this Agreement.
192: 
193: **[ARTICLE 5 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY]{.underline}**
194: 
195: **Section 5.1 --- Vendor IP Ownership**
196: 
197: As between the Parties, Vendor is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to: (a) the Platform; (b) the Base Model; (c) all Fine-Tuned Weights; (d) all Customer-Trained Adaptations; (e) all Derivative Models; and (f) all improvements, enhancements, updates, upgrades, modifications, and derivative works of any of the foregoing, together with all Intellectual Property Rights therein and thereto, regardless of whether such items are created by Vendor independently, in collaboration with Customer, or through the processing of Customer Data. For the avoidance of doubt, all fine-tuned weights, adapter layers, prompt-tuning parameters, and similar derivative model parameters generated through the fine-tuning, training, or adaptation of the Base Model using Customer Data shall be considered Derivative Models and are owned exclusively by Vendor. Customer hereby assigns, and agrees to assign, to Vendor all right, title, and interest that Customer may have or acquire in any Derivative Models, Customer-Trained Adaptations, or Fine-Tuned Weights, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and agrees to execute such documents and take such further actions as may be reasonably necessary to effectuate and perfect such assignment.
198: 
199: **Section 5.2 --- Customer Data Ownership**
200: 
201: As between the Parties, Customer is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to all Customer Data, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. Vendor\'s right to access, use, and process Customer Data is limited to the purposes expressly set forth in this Agreement, including providing the Platform, performing the Implementation Services, and the service improvement purposes described in Section 6.1. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as transferring ownership of Customer Data from Customer to Vendor. Vendor acknowledges that Customer Data may contain NPPI and other regulated data, and Vendor agrees to treat all Customer Data in accordance with its obligations under this Agreement and applicable law.
202: 
203: **Section 5.3 --- Feedback**
204: 
205: If Customer or any of its employees, contractors, or agents provides any suggestions, enhancement requests, ideas, recommendations, corrections, or other feedback regarding the Platform, the Documentation, or any of Vendor\'s products or services (collectively, \"**Feedback**\"), Customer hereby grants to Vendor a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, transferable, sublicensable license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works from, distribute, display, perform, and otherwise exploit such Feedback in any manner and for any purpose, without restriction, attribution, or compensation to Customer. Customer acknowledges that Vendor may use Feedback to improve the Platform, develop new features, or create new products or services, and that Vendor shall have no obligation to implement or incorporate any Feedback.
206: 
207: **Section 5.4 --- No Other Rights**
208: 
209: Except as expressly set forth in this Article 5 and the license granted in Section 2.1, neither Party grants the other Party any right, title, or interest in or to its Intellectual Property Rights, whether by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any rights in Vendor\'s trade secrets, proprietary algorithms, model architectures, training methodologies, or other confidential technical information, except as expressly provided herein.
210: 
211: **[ARTICLE 6 --- DATA PROCESSING AND PRIVACY]{.underline}**
212: 
213: **Section 6.1 --- Customer Data Processing**
214: 
215: Vendor shall process Customer Data solely for the following purposes: (a) providing the Platform and performing Vendor\'s obligations under this Agreement, including the Implementation Services; (b) operating, maintaining, supporting, and securing the Platform; and (c) service improvement purposes, including but not limited to improving the Base Model, developing new features and capabilities, training and validating Derivative Models, and conducting research and development related to Vendor\'s artificial intelligence products and services. For purposes of clause (c), Vendor may process Customer Data in de-identified and aggregated form such that the data does not identify or permit identification of Customer or any individual. Vendor shall implement appropriate technical measures to de-identify and aggregate Customer Data prior to its use for service improvement purposes. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data to any third party or use Customer Data for any purpose other than as expressly set forth in this Section 6.1.
216: 
217: **Section 6.2 --- Controller Status**
218: 
219: Each Party acknowledges that it acts as an independent data controller with respect to its own processing activities relating to Customer Data under this Agreement. Customer is the data controller with respect to Customer Data as it relates to Customer\'s internal business operations and its provision of Customer Data to Vendor. Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data for the purpose of providing the Platform under Section 6.1(a) and (b) shall be undertaken by Vendor on behalf of Customer. Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data for service improvement purposes under Section 6.1(c) shall be undertaken by Vendor as an independent data controller, and Vendor shall independently determine the purposes and means of such processing. Each Party shall be individually responsible for complying with its obligations under applicable data protection and privacy laws with respect to its processing activities as a data controller.
220: 
221: **Section 6.3 --- Compliance with Laws**
222: 
223: Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws, rules, and regulations in connection with its processing of Customer Data under this Agreement, including without limitation: (a) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 6801--6809, and its implementing regulations, including Regulation S-P (17 C.F.R. Part 248) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) (\"**GLBA**\"), to the extent applicable to the processing of NPPI; (b) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.100--1798.199.100 (\"**CCPA/CPRA**\"), to the extent applicable; and (c) any other applicable federal, state, or international data protection or privacy laws. To the extent required by applicable law, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to enter into any additional data processing agreements or addenda necessary to comply with applicable data protection requirements.
224: 
225: **Section 6.4 --- Security Measures**
226: 
227: Vendor shall implement and maintain throughout the Term commercially reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction, consistent with industry standards for cloud-based enterprise software providers. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor\'s security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer\'s reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor\'s then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor\'s information security controls.
228: 
229: **Section 6.5 --- Data Breach Notification**
230: 
231: In the event of any confirmed security breach involving the unauthorized access, acquisition, use, or disclosure of Customer Data (a \"**Security Breach**\"), Vendor shall: (a) notify Customer of the Security Breach without unreasonable delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation of the Security Breach; (b) promptly investigate the Security Breach and take reasonable steps to contain, mitigate, and remediate the Security Breach; (c) provide Customer with reasonably detailed information regarding the nature and scope of the Security Breach, including the categories and approximate number of records affected, the likely consequences of the Security Breach, and the measures taken or proposed to address and mitigate the Security Breach; and (d) cooperate with Customer in Customer\'s investigation, response, and notification obligations in connection with the Security Breach. The obligations set forth in this Section 6.5 shall not be construed as an acknowledgment by Vendor of any fault or liability with respect to the Security Breach.
232: 
233: **Section 6.6 --- Return and Deletion of Data**
234: 
235: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer\'s written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Vendor shall complete such return or deletion within sixty (60) calendar days of receipt of Customer\'s written request. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6.6. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor may retain copies of Customer Data to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or legal hold obligation, provided that Vendor continues to protect such retained data in accordance with this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, data that has been de-identified and aggregated for service improvement purposes in accordance with Section 6.1 shall not constitute Customer Data for purposes of this Section 6.6 and shall not be subject to the return or deletion obligations set forth herein.
236: 
237: **[ARTICLE 7 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
238: 
239: **Section 7.1 --- Definition of Confidential Information**
240: 
241: \"**Confidential Information**\" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"**Disclosing Party**\") to the other Party (the \"**Receiving Party**\") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as \"confidential,\" \"proprietary,\" or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Any changes to the scope, timeline, deliverables, or fees for Implementation Services shall be documented in a mutually agreed written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No change to the Implementation Services shall be binding unless set forth in a duly executed change order. Each change order shall specify the nature of the change, any impact on the project timeline and milestones, and any additional fees associated with the change. Vendor shall not be obligated to perform any work outside the scope of an executed Statement of Work or change order.
**[ARTICLE 4 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**
**Section 4.1 --- Annual Platform Fee**

In consideration of the license and access rights granted hereunder, Customer shall pay to Vendor an annual platform fee of Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,400,000) per Contract Year (the \"**Annual Platform Fee**\"). The Annual Platform Fee shall be invoiced by Vendor in equal monthly installments of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$200,000) per month, with each monthly invoice due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice. Vendor shall issue monthly invoices on or about the first business day of each calendar month during the Term, beginning with the first calendar month following the Effective Date.
**Section 4.2 --- Implementation Fee**

In consideration of the Implementation Services described in Article 3 and Exhibit A, Customer shall pay to Vendor a one-time implementation and fine-tuning fee of Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$850,000) (the \"**Implementation Fee**\"). The Implementation Fee shall be payable in two (2) equal installments of Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000) each, as follows:

> \(a\) **First Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following execution of the Initial SOW (Milestone 1).
> \(b\) **Second Installment.** Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000), due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice following achievement of Go-Live (Milestone 2).
**Section 4.3 --- Overage Fees**

The Annual Platform Fee includes forty million (40,000,000) API calls per Contract Year (the \"**Included API Calls**\"). API calls made by Customer in excess of the Included API Calls during any Contract Year shall be invoiced by Vendor at a rate of twelve-thousandths of a dollar (\$0.012) per API call (the \"**Overage Rate**\"). Overage Fees shall be invoiced monthly in arrears, based on Vendor\'s metering and usage data for the applicable calendar month. Each such invoice shall include a summary of API call usage for the month, including the number of API calls consumed and the number of remaining Included API Calls for the applicable Contract Year. Overage Fee invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.
**Section 4.4 --- Taxes**

All Fees set forth in this Agreement are exclusive of any and all applicable taxes, duties, levies, or similar governmental charges (collectively, \"**Taxes**\"). Customer shall be responsible for, and shall pay, all sales, use, value-added, goods and services, withholding, and similar Taxes imposed on or in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, excluding taxes based on Vendor\'s net income, capital, or franchise taxes assessed against Vendor. If Vendor is required by law to collect any Taxes from Customer, Vendor shall include such Taxes on the applicable invoice and Customer shall remit payment of such Taxes together with the applicable Fees. If Customer is required to withhold any Taxes from amounts payable to Vendor, Customer shall gross up the payment so that Vendor receives the full amount of the invoiced Fees after deduction of such withholding Taxes.
**Section 4.5 --- Late Payments**

Any undisputed Fees not paid when due shall accrue interest at the lesser of (a) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (18% per annum) or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received in full by Vendor. In addition, Vendor may, upon at least fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice to Customer, suspend Customer\'s access to the Platform if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than forty-five (45) days past its due date, and such suspension shall continue until all outstanding amounts, including accrued interest, have been paid in full. The foregoing remedies are in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other remedies available to Vendor under this Agreement or applicable law.
**Section 4.6 --- Total Contract Value**
For informational purposes and clarity, the total contract value for the Initial Term (exclusive of Overage Fees and Taxes) is as follows:
> \(a\) Annual Platform Fees for three (3) Contract Years: \$2,400,000 × 3 = **\$7,200,000**;
> \(b\) Implementation Fee (one-time): **\$850,000**;

The foregoing total contract value is an estimate for informational purposes only and does not include any Overage Fees, Taxes, or fees for additional Statements of Work that may be executed during the Term. The total contract value does not limit Vendor\'s right to invoice for Overage Fees or other amounts payable under this Agreement.
**[ARTICLE 5 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY]{.underline}**
**Section 5.1 --- Vendor IP Ownership**

As between the Parties, Vendor is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to: (a) the Platform; (b) the Base Model; (c) all Fine-Tuned Weights; (d) all Customer-Trained Adaptations; (e) all Derivative Models; and (f) all improvements, enhancements, updates, upgrades, modifications, and derivative works of any of the foregoing, together with all Intellectual Property Rights therein and thereto, regardless of whether such items are created by Vendor independently, in collaboration with Customer, or through the processing of Customer Data. For the avoidance of doubt, all fine-tuned weights, adapter layers, prompt-tuning parameters, and similar derivative model parameters generated through the fine-tuning, training, or adaptation of the Base Model using Customer Data shall be considered Derivative Models and are owned exclusively by Vendor. Customer hereby assigns, and agrees to assign, to Vendor all right, title, and interest that Customer may have or acquire in any Derivative Models, Customer-Trained Adaptations, or Fine-Tuned Weights, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and agrees to execute such documents and take such further actions as may be reasonably necessary to effectuate and perfect such assignment.
**Section 5.2 --- Customer Data Ownership**

As between the Parties, Customer is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to all Customer Data, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. Vendor\'s right to access, use, and process Customer Data is limited to the purposes expressly set forth in this Agreement, including providing the Platform, performing the Implementation Services, and the service improvement purposes described in Section 6.1. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as transferring ownership of Customer Data from Customer to Vendor. Vendor acknowledges that Customer Data may contain NPPI and other regulated data, and Vendor agrees to treat all Customer Data in accordance with its obligations under this Agreement and applicable law.
**Section 5.3 --- Feedback**

If Customer or any of its employees, contractors, or agents provides any suggestions, enhancement requests, ideas, recommendations, corrections, or other feedback regarding the Platform, the Documentation, or any of Vendor\'s products or services (collectively, \"**Feedback**\"), Customer hereby grants to Vendor a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, transferable, sublicensable license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works from, distribute, display, perform, and otherwise exploit such Feedback in any manner and for any purpose, without restriction, attribution, or compensation to Customer. Customer acknowledges that Vendor may use Feedback to improve the Platform, develop new features, or create new products or services, and that Vendor shall have no obligation to implement or incorporate any Feedback.
**Section 5.4 --- No Other Rights**

Except as expressly set forth in this Article 5 and the license granted in Section 2.1, neither Party grants the other Party any right, title, or interest in or to its Intellectual Property Rights, whether by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any rights in Vendor\'s trade secrets, proprietary algorithms, model architectures, training methodologies, or other confidential technical information, except as expressly provided herein.
**[ARTICLE 6 --- DATA PROCESSING AND PRIVACY]{.underline}**
**Section 6.1 --- Customer Data Processing**

Vendor shall process Customer Data solely for the following purposes: (a) providing the Platform and performing Vendor\'s obligations under this Agreement, including the Implementation Services; (b) operating, maintaining, supporting, and securing the Platform; and (c) service improvement purposes, including but not limited to improving the Base Model, developing new features and capabilities, training and validating Derivative Models, and conducting research and development related to Vendor\'s artificial intelligence products and services. For purposes of clause (c), Vendor may process Customer Data in de-identified and aggregated form such that the data does not identify or permit identification of Customer or any individual. Vendor shall implement appropriate technical measures to de-identify and aggregate Customer Data prior to its use for service improvement purposes. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data to any third party or use Customer Data for any purpose other than as expressly set forth in this Section 6.1.
**Section 6.2 --- Controller Status**

Each Party acknowledges that it acts as an independent data controller with respect to its own processing activities relating to Customer Data under this Agreement. Customer is the data controller with respect to Customer Data as it relates to Customer\'s internal business operations and its provision of Customer Data to Vendor. Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data for the purpose of providing the Platform under Section 6.1(a) and (b) shall be undertaken by Vendor on behalf of Customer. Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data for service improvement purposes under Section 6.1(c) shall be undertaken by Vendor as an independent data controller, and Vendor shall independently determine the purposes and means of such processing. Each Party shall be individually responsible for complying with its obligations under applicable data protection and privacy laws with respect to its processing activities as a data controller.
**Section 6.3 --- Compliance with Laws**

Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws, rules, and regulations in connection with its processing of Customer Data under this Agreement, including without limitation: (a) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 6801--6809, and its implementing regulations, including Regulation S-P (17 C.F.R. Part 248) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) (\"**GLBA**\"), to the extent applicable to the processing of NPPI; (b) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.100--1798.199.100 (\"**CCPA/CPRA**\"), to the extent applicable; and (c) any other applicable federal, state, or international data protection or privacy laws. To the extent required by applicable law, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to enter into any additional data processing agreements or addenda necessary to comply with applicable data protection requirements.
**Section 6.4 --- Security Measures**

Vendor shall implement and maintain throughout the Term commercially reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction, consistent with industry standards for cloud-based enterprise software providers. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor\'s security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer\'s reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor\'s then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor\'s information security controls.
**Section 6.5 --- Data Breach Notification**

In the event of any confirmed security breach involving the unauthorized access, acquisition, use, or disclosure of Customer Data (a \"**Security Breach**\"), Vendor shall: (a) notify Customer of the Security Breach without unreasonable delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation of the Security Breach; (b) promptly investigate the Security Breach and take reasonable steps to contain, mitigate, and remediate the Security Breach; (c) provide Customer with reasonably detailed information regarding the nature and scope of the Security Breach, including the categories and approximate number of records affected, the likely consequences of the Security Breach, and the measures taken or proposed to address and mitigate the Security Breach; and (d) cooperate with Customer in Customer\'s investigation, response, and notification obligations in connection with the Security Breach. The obligations set forth in this Section 6.5 shall not be construed as an acknowledgment by Vendor of any fault or liability with respect to the Security Breach.
**Section 6.6 --- Return and Deletion of Data**

Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer\'s written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Vendor shall complete such return or deletion within sixty (60) calendar days of receipt of Customer\'s written request. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6.6. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor may retain copies of Customer Data to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or legal hold obligation, provided that Vendor continues to protect such retained data in accordance with this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, data that has been de-identified and aggregated for service improvement purposes in accordance with Section 6.1 shall not constitute Customer Data for purposes of this Section 6.6 and shall not be subject to the return or deletion obligations set forth herein.
**[ARTICLE 7 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
**Section 7.1 --- Definition of Confidential Information**

\"**Confidential Information**\" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"**Disclosing Party**\") to the other Party (the \"**Receiving Party**\") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as \"confidential,\" \"proprietary,\" or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes: (a) business plans, strategies, forecasts, and financial information; (b) technical information, including source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, training data, APIs, and system designs; (c) trade secrets; (d) customer lists, supplier lists, and pricing information; (e) product roadmaps and development plans; and (f) the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all pricing, fee, and commercial terms. Customer Data shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer regardless of whether it is marked or designated as confidential.

Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records.
**Section 7.2 --- Obligations**

The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information using commercially reasonable measures that are at least as protective as those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the expiration or termination of this Agreement; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.
**Section 7.3 --- Permitted Disclosures**

The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, \"**Authorized Recipients**\"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.

The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party\'s expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.
**[ARTICLE 8 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**
**Section 8.1 --- Mutual Representations and Warranties**
Each Party hereby represents and warrants to the other Party as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Effective Date that:
> \(a\) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation;
> \(b\) it has full corporate or limited liability company power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder;
> \(c\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or limited liability company action;

> \(d\) this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and

> \(e\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party\'s organizational documents, (ii) violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Party is a party or by which it is bound.
**Section 8.2 --- Vendor Representations and Warranties**
Vendor hereby represents and warrants to Customer that:

> \(a\) the Platform, when used in accordance with the Documentation and this Agreement, will perform materially in accordance with the functional specifications set forth in the Documentation during the Term;

> \(b\) the Implementation Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards for similar services, using personnel with the requisite skill, experience, and qualifications;

> \(c\) Vendor has all rights necessary to grant the license set forth in Section 2.1, free and clear of any liens, encumbrances, or restrictions that would materially impair Customer\'s exercise of the rights granted thereunder; and

> \(d\) to Vendor\'s knowledge as of the Effective Date, the Platform, as provided by Vendor and used in accordance with this Agreement, does not infringe any registered United States patent or registered United States copyright of any third party.

Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any breach of the warranty set forth in Section 8.2(a) shall be for Vendor, at its option, to (i) repair or replace the non-conforming Platform functionality so that it conforms to the Documentation, or (ii) if Vendor is unable to repair or replace such functionality within a commercially reasonable period, terminate this Agreement and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.
**Section 8.3 --- Disclaimer**

EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 8, VENDOR MAKES NO WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, WITH RESPECT TO THE PLATFORM, THE IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES, THE BASE MODEL, ANY DERIVATIVE MODELS, OR ANY OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, TITLE, ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS, RELIABILITY, OR QUALITY OF OUTPUTS. VENDOR DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL BE ERROR-FREE, UNINTERRUPTED, OR FREE OF HARMFUL COMPONENTS, OR THAT THE OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM WILL BE ACCURATE, COMPLETE, OR SUITABLE FOR ANY PARTICULAR PURPOSE. CUSTOMER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS ARE PROBABILISTIC IN NATURE AND THAT OUTPUTS MAY CONTAIN ERRORS, HALLUCINATIONS, OR INACCURACIES, AND CUSTOMER IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR EVALUATING AND VALIDATING ALL OUTPUTS FOR ITS INTENDED USE.
**[ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS]{.underline}**
**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and nine-tenths percent (99.9%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).
**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain API response latency at or below six hundred (600) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 600 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety (F1 ≥ 0.90), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.
**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA in any calendar month, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the Uptime SLA failure occurred.

Service Credits constitute Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any failure to meet the service level commitments set forth in this Article 9. Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement and shall not be refundable in cash. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year.
**Section 9.5 --- Reporting**

Vendor shall provide Customer with monthly reports detailing Platform uptime, API latency, and model accuracy metrics for the preceding calendar month. Such reports shall be delivered to Customer within ten (10) business days following the end of each calendar month. Reports shall include, at a minimum: (a) Platform availability percentage; (b) total Downtime minutes and the cause of each incident; (c) API latency at the 50th percentile (p50) and 95th percentile (p95); (d) model accuracy metrics, including F1 score, precision, and recall, as measured against the validation dataset; and (e) API call usage data, including the total number of API calls consumed during the month and the cumulative total for the current Contract Year. Vendor shall make authorized Customer personnel available for a monthly service review meeting, upon Customer\'s reasonable request, to discuss the monthly reports and any performance issues.
**[ARTICLE 10 --- LIMITATION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**
**Section 10.1 --- Exclusion of Consequential Damages**

IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF GOODWILL, LOSS OF DATA, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, OR ANY OTHER COMMERCIAL DAMAGES OR LOSSES, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES OR COULD HAVE FORESEEN SUCH DAMAGES. THE FOREGOING EXCLUSION SHALL APPLY REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SUCH DAMAGES ARISE FROM BREACH OF CONTRACT, BREACH OF WARRANTY, TORT, OR ANY OTHER CAUSE OF ACTION.
**Section 10.2 --- Aggregate Liability Cap**

EXCEPT AS SET FORTH IN SECTION 10.3, EACH PARTY\'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO VENDOR DURING THE SIX (6)-MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE DATE OF THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM. FOR CLARITY, BASED ON THE ANNUAL PLATFORM FEE, THIS LIABILITY CAP EQUALS ONE MILLION TWO HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS (\$1,200,000).
**Section 10.3 --- Exclusions from Cap**

The limitations and exclusions set forth in Sections 10.1 and 10.2 shall not apply to: (a) Customer\'s payment obligations under Article 4; (b) either Party\'s obligations under Article 7 (Confidentiality); (c) either Party\'s indemnification obligations under Article 11; (d) liability arising from a Party\'s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; or (e) liability arising from Vendor\'s breach of Section 6.4 (Security Measures) or Section 6.5 (Data Breach Notification) to the extent involving Vendor\'s gross negligence or willful misconduct.
**[ARTICLE 11 --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**
**Section 11.1 --- Vendor Indemnification**

Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"**Customer Indemnitees**\") from and against any third-party claim, suit, action, or proceeding alleging that Customer\'s authorized use of the Platform in accordance with this Agreement constitutes direct infringement of a registered United States patent or a registered United States copyright (each, an \"**IP Claim**\"), and shall pay all damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction or agreed to in settlement of such IP Claim.

Vendor\'s obligations under this Section 11.1 are expressly limited to claims of direct infringement of registered United States patents and registered United States copyrights. Vendor shall have no indemnification obligation with respect to any claim based on or arising from:
> \(i\) trade secrets, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, or unregistered intellectual property rights of any kind;
> \(ii\) indirect infringement, contributory infringement, or inducement of infringement;

> \(iii\) Customer\'s combination of the Platform with any third-party products, services, hardware, software, data, or content not provided by Vendor, to the extent such combination gives rise to the infringement claim;
> \(iv\) Customer\'s modification, alteration, or customization of the Platform or its outputs, to the extent such modification gives rise to the infringement claim;
> \(v\) Customer\'s use of the Platform in violation of this Agreement, the Documentation, or applicable law;
> \(vi\) Customer\'s use of a version of the Platform other than the then-current version, if the infringement would have been avoided by use of the then-current version made available by Vendor; or
> \(vii\) any output generated by the Platform, to the extent the infringement claim relates to the content of such output rather than the Platform itself.
**Section 11.2 --- Vendor Remediation**
If the Platform becomes, or in Vendor\'s reasonable opinion is likely to become, the subject of an IP Claim, Vendor may, at its sole option and expense:
> \(a\) procure for Customer the right to continue using the Platform under terms substantially consistent with this Agreement;

> \(b\) modify or replace the Platform (or the infringing component thereof) to make it non-infringing, provided that such modification or replacement does not materially diminish the functionality of the Platform; or

> \(c\) if neither clause (a) nor clause (b) is commercially practicable in Vendor\'s reasonable determination, terminate this Agreement upon written notice to Customer and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.

The remedies set forth in this Section 11.2, together with the indemnification obligations set forth in Section 11.1, shall constitute Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, with respect to any IP Claim.
**Section 11.3 --- Customer Indemnification**

Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor and its members, managers, officers, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"**Vendor Indemnitees**\") from and against any third-party claim, suit, action, or proceeding arising from or relating to:
