9: **[I. Escrow Service Overview]{.underline}**
10: 
11: Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. (\"Iron Mountain IPM\" or \"Escrow Agent\") provides a standard three-party technology escrow service designed to safeguard the interests of licensees and customers of proprietary technology. The escrow arrangement ensures that critical technology assets --- including, without limitation, source code, machine-learning model weights, training data configurations, and related technical documentation --- are deposited with a neutral, independent escrow agent and held securely for the benefit of a designated beneficiary. In the event that specified release conditions occur, the deposited materials are made available to the beneficiary so that the beneficiary may continue to use, maintain, and operate the technology in accordance with the rights granted under the underlying license or vendor agreement.
12: 
13: The Iron Mountain IPM technology escrow service is widely recognized as an industry-standard mechanism for mitigating the risks associated with dependence on a single technology vendor. By requiring the vendor (the \"Depositor\") to place current and complete copies of the technology in escrow, the arrangement provides meaningful assurance to the licensee (the \"Beneficiary\") that it will retain the ability to access, maintain, and, where applicable, reconstruct the deposited technology in the event the Depositor is unable or unwilling to continue providing support, maintenance, or access to the technology.
14: 
15: **This summary is provided for reference and informational purposes only.** It is intended to facilitate internal review and evaluation by TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"TechNova\" or \"Beneficiary\") in connection with the proposed escrow arrangement involving Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"Meridian\" or \"Depositor\"). The governing terms of the escrow arrangement will be set forth exclusively in a fully executed Technology Escrow Agreement (the \"Escrow Agreement\") among the three parties --- Iron Mountain IPM, Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC, and TechNova Solutions, Inc. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between this summary and the executed Escrow Agreement, the terms of the executed Escrow Agreement shall control in all respects.
16: 
17: **[II. Parties]{.underline}**
18: 
19: The Technology Escrow Agreement contemplates the following three parties, each of which has distinct rights and obligations under the arrangement:
20: 
21: **Depositor (Vendor):** The owner or licensor of the deposited technology. The Depositor is responsible for delivering complete and current copies of all deposit materials to the Escrow Agent, maintaining and updating the deposit in accordance with the agreed-upon schedule, and cooperating with any verification processes specified in the Escrow Agreement. For purposes of this summary, the anticipated Depositor is:
22: 
23: > **Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC** A Delaware limited liability company
24: 
25: Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC is the owner and licensor of the proprietary cognitive analytics platform and associated machine-learning models licensed to TechNova Solutions, Inc. under the parties\' underlying Master Software License and Services Agreement. Meridian will be responsible for depositing and maintaining all specified technology assets in escrow in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement.
26: 
27: **Beneficiary (Customer):** The licensee or customer entitled to receive copies of the deposited materials upon the occurrence of a qualifying release event. The Beneficiary has the right to request release of the deposit materials, to request verification of the completeness and accuracy of the deposit, and to receive notice of certain events relating to the escrow arrangement. For purposes of this summary, the anticipated Beneficiary is:
28: 
29: > **TechNova Solutions, Inc.** A California corporation Internal Reference No.: TNS-VENDOR-2025-0043
30: 
31: TechNova Solutions, Inc. is the licensee of Meridian\'s proprietary technology and will be designated as the sole initial beneficiary under the Escrow Agreement. Additional beneficiaries may be added to the arrangement in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement and subject to the payment of applicable additional-beneficiary fees as set forth in Section VIII below.
32: 
33: **Escrow Agent:** The independent, neutral third party responsible for receiving, securely storing, and, upon the occurrence of specified release conditions or as otherwise directed, releasing the deposited materials. The Escrow Agent has no ownership interest in the deposited materials and acts solely in a custodial and administrative capacity. The Escrow Agent for this arrangement is:
34: 
35: > **Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc.** A subsidiary of Iron Mountain Incorporated
36: 
37: Iron Mountain IPM maintains secure, geographically redundant storage facilities and employs industry-standard security protocols to protect the confidentiality and integrity of all deposited materials throughout the term of the escrow arrangement. Iron Mountain IPM\'s obligations are limited to those expressly set forth in the Escrow Agreement, and Iron Mountain IPM does not assume any obligations under the underlying license or vendor agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary.
38: 
39: **[III. Deposit Materials]{.underline}**
40: 
41: The deposit scope encompasses the following categories of technology assets, as applicable to the deposited technology and as further specified in the deposit description schedule to be attached to the Escrow Agreement. The parties acknowledge that the completeness and utility of the deposit depend on the inclusion of all materials reasonably necessary for a qualified technical professional to understand, compile, build, deploy, and maintain the deposited technology.
42: 
43: The standard deposit scope includes:
44: 
45: **A. Source Code.** Complete and current source code for all modules, libraries, components, and build scripts comprising or required to build the deposited technology, including but not limited to:
46: 
47: > • All application source code files, organized in the same directory and project structure used by Depositor\'s development team;
48: >
49: > • All third-party libraries, frameworks, and dependencies included in or required by the build process, to the extent Depositor has the right to include such materials (or, where redistribution is not permitted, identification of all required third-party components together with version numbers and download or acquisition instructions);
50: >
51: > • All build scripts, makefiles, configuration files, and continuous-integration/continuous-deployment (CI/CD) pipeline definitions necessary to compile, link, and package the deposited technology into deployable form;
52: >
53: > • All automated test suites, test scripts, test data, and test harnesses included in the Depositor\'s standard development environment.
54: 
55: **B. Model Weights.** All machine-learning model weights associated with the deposited technology, including:
56: 
57: > • Base model weights for all foundational models used by the deposited technology;
58: >
59: > • Fine-tuned adapter weights (e.g., LoRA, QLoRA, or similar parameter-efficient fine-tuning artifacts) and any associated configuration files specifying adapter architecture, rank, and merging instructions;
60: >
61: > • Model checkpoint files for each production-release version of the deposited technology;
62: >
63: > • Tokenizer vocabularies, embedding matrices, and any custom model components necessary to load and execute the deposited models.
64: 
65: The specific model weights to be deposited shall be identified by mutual agreement of Depositor and Beneficiary and set forth in the deposit description schedule. Where the deposited technology incorporates third-party base models subject to separate license terms, the Depositor shall identify those models and provide copies of the applicable license terms to the extent necessary for the Beneficiary to understand the scope of rights available upon release.
66: 
67: **C. Training Data Configurations and Pipeline Artifacts.** All configurations, scripts, and artifacts necessary to understand and, where feasible, reproduce the training pipeline for the deposited models, including:
68: 
69: > • Hyperparameter specifications for each training run associated with a production-release model;
70: >
71: > • Data preprocessing scripts, data cleaning pipelines, and feature-engineering code;
72: >
73: > • Training configuration files (e.g., YAML, JSON, or TOML files specifying training parameters, optimizer settings, learning rate schedules, and data augmentation strategies);
74: >
75: > • Data pipeline orchestration scripts and workflow definitions;
76: >
77: > • Evaluation scripts, metrics definitions, and benchmark results for each deposited model version.
78: 
79: For the avoidance of doubt, the deposit of training data configurations and pipeline artifacts does not necessarily require the deposit of the underlying raw training data itself. The inclusion or exclusion of raw training data shall be determined by mutual agreement of Depositor and Beneficiary, taking into account data licensing restrictions, data volume, and the practical requirements for maintaining and retraining the deposited models. Where raw training data is not included, Depositor shall provide sufficient documentation to identify all training data sources, describe any licensing or access requirements, and enable the Beneficiary to obtain the necessary data independently.
80: 
81: **D. Technical Documentation.** Comprehensive technical documentation sufficient to enable a qualified technical professional to understand, build, deploy, configure, and maintain the deposited technology, including:
82: 
83: > • Build instructions providing step-by-step procedures for compiling, building, and packaging the deposited technology from source in a clean development environment;
84: >
85: > • Architecture diagrams depicting the high-level and component-level architecture of the deposited technology, including data flow diagrams, system integration points, and infrastructure requirements;
86: >
87: > • Deployment guides describing the procedures and requirements for deploying the deposited technology in production and non-production environments, including hardware and software prerequisites, environment configuration, and security settings;
88: >
89: > • Dependency manifests listing all third-party software components, libraries, frameworks, services, and tools required by the deposited technology, together with version numbers, license types, and acquisition instructions;
90: >
91: > • API documentation for all internal and external interfaces;
92: >
93: > • Database schemas, migration scripts, and data dictionary documentation;
94: >
95: > • Operations and maintenance guides, including monitoring, logging, backup, and disaster-recovery procedures.
96: 
97: **E. Additional Materials.** Any additional materials specified in the underlying Master Software License and Services Agreement or other vendor agreement between Depositor and Beneficiary, or as otherwise agreed in writing by the parties and set forth in the deposit description schedule attached to the Escrow Agreement. Such additional materials may include, by way of example and not limitation, encryption keys, digital certificates, hardware security module (HSM) configurations, container images, infrastructure-as-code templates, and environment-specific configuration files.
98: 
99: **Format Requirements.** All deposit materials shall be delivered in industry-standard, machine-readable formats agreed upon by the parties. Source code and scripts shall be delivered in their native file formats (e.g., .py, .java, .js, .go, .rs, .cpp, .h, .yaml, .json, .toml). Model weights shall be delivered in widely supported serialization formats (e.g., PyTorch .pt/.pth, TensorFlow SavedModel, ONNX, SafeTensors). Documentation shall be delivered in portable formats (e.g., PDF, Markdown, HTML). The Depositor shall include a top-level README file providing an index and description of all deposited materials.
100: 
101: **[IV. Deposit and Update Requirements]{.underline}**
102: 
103: Timely and regular deposits are essential to ensure that the escrowed materials remain current and useful in the event of a release. The Escrow Agreement will establish the following deposit and update obligations:
104: 
105: **A. Initial Deposit.** The Depositor shall deliver a complete initial deposit of all deposit materials described in Section III above to the Escrow Agent within thirty (30) calendar days following the date of full execution of the Escrow Agreement by all three parties. The initial deposit shall include all materials corresponding to the then-current production release version of the deposited technology as of the date of the Escrow Agreement.
106: 
107: The Depositor shall accompany each deposit (including the initial deposit) with a completed deposit description form, in the format prescribed by Iron Mountain IPM, identifying the materials included in the deposit, the version or release number of the deposited technology, the date of the deposit, and a manifest listing all files and directories included in the deposit together with file sizes and checksums (e.g., SHA-256 hashes) sufficient to verify file integrity.
108: 
109: **B. Update Frequency.** Following the initial deposit, the Depositor shall update the deposit materials on a regular and ongoing basis throughout the term of the Escrow Agreement. At a minimum, the Depositor shall deliver an updated deposit:
110: 
111: > • No less frequently than once per calendar quarter (i.e., at least four updates per calendar year); or
112: >
113: > • Within fifteen (15) business days following each major release, minor release, or material update to the deposited technology that is made available to the Beneficiary under the underlying agreement,
114: 
115: whichever results in more frequent updates. For purposes of this requirement, a \"material update\" includes any update that introduces new functionality, modifies the model architecture, retrains or fine-tunes model weights, changes the build or deployment process in a manner that would affect the Beneficiary\'s ability to build or deploy the technology, or addresses a critical security vulnerability.
116: 
117: Each updated deposit shall constitute a complete replacement of the prior deposit or, at the Depositor\'s option, a clearly documented incremental update together with instructions for integrating the incremental update with the prior deposit to produce a complete and current set of deposit materials.
118: 
119: **C. Deposit Media and Delivery Method.** All deposits shall be delivered via secure electronic transfer to Iron Mountain IPM\'s designated secure repository. Iron Mountain IPM will provide the Depositor with access credentials and transfer instructions upon execution of the Escrow Agreement. Electronic transfers shall be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and shall be encrypted at rest within Iron Mountain IPM\'s storage infrastructure.
120: 
121: Physical media deposits (e.g., encrypted USB drives, encrypted hard drives) will be accepted upon request, provided that the Depositor coordinates delivery logistics with Iron Mountain IPM in advance and that all physical media are encrypted using AES-256 or equivalent encryption, with decryption keys delivered separately to Iron Mountain IPM via a secure, out-of-band channel.
122: 
123: **D. Depositor Certifications.** With each deposit, the Depositor shall certify in writing that: (i) the deposited materials are complete and current as of the date of deposit; (ii) the deposited materials correspond to the version of the technology identified in the deposit description form; (iii) the Depositor has the right to deposit the materials with the Escrow Agent for the purposes contemplated by the Escrow Agreement; and (iv) the deposited materials, together with the accompanying documentation, are sufficient to enable a qualified technical professional to build, deploy, and maintain the deposited technology.
124: 
125: **[V. Verification Services]{.underline}**
126: 
127: Iron Mountain IPM offers optional technical verification services designed to confirm that the deposited materials are complete, readable, and, at the highest verification tier, operationally functional. Verification provides an important layer of assurance to the Beneficiary that the deposited materials will be useful and usable in the event of a release.
128: 
129: Iron Mountain IPM\'s verification services are available at three tiers, described below in order of increasing depth and rigor:
130: 
131: **Level 1 --- Inventory Verification**
132: 
133: Level 1 verification provides a baseline confirmation that the deposited files match the deposit description and manifest provided by the Depositor. The Level 1 verification process includes the following:
134: 
135: > • Comparison of the files and directories received against the file manifest and deposit description form submitted by the Depositor;
136: >
137: > • Confirmation that the number, names, and organization of deposited files are consistent with the manifest;
138: >
139: > • Verification of file integrity through checksum comparison (e.g., SHA-256 hash verification);
140: >
141: > • Identification of any discrepancies between the manifest and the actual deposit contents.
142: 
143: Upon completion of Level 1 verification, Iron Mountain IPM will provide a written verification report to both Depositor and Beneficiary identifying any discrepancies and confirming whether the deposit contents match the manifest. Level 1 verification does not include any assessment of file readability, format correctness, content completeness, or technical functionality.
144: 
145: **Level 2 --- Technical Review**
146: 
147: Level 2 verification provides a more thorough assessment of deposit completeness and readability. In addition to all steps included in Level 1 verification, the Level 2 process includes:
148: 
149: > • Confirmation that all deposited files can be opened and read using appropriate software tools;
150: >
151: > • Verification that deposited files are in the stated file formats and are not corrupted, truncated, or otherwise unreadable;
152: >
153: > • Review of the deposit for the presence of required build and deployment documentation, including build instructions, dependency manifests, and architecture documentation;
154: >
155: > • Assessment of overall deposit organization and completeness relative to the deposit description and the stated scope of the deposited technology;
156: >
157: > • Identification of any apparent gaps, missing components, or incomplete documentation.
158: 
159: Upon completion of Level 2 verification, Iron Mountain IPM will provide a detailed written verification report identifying the results of each verification step, including any identified gaps, deficiencies, or areas of concern. Level 2 verification does not include any attempt to compile, build, or execute the deposited technology.
160: 
161: **Iron Mountain IPM recommends Level 2 verification at minimum for deposits involving machine-learning model weights and training configurations.** Deposits of this nature are inherently complex and may involve large binary files, specialized serialization formats, and interdependencies among model components, training artifacts, and deployment infrastructure. Level 2 verification helps to ensure that the deposited materials are readable and organized in a manner that would be useful to the Beneficiary in the event of a release, and that critical components such as model weight files, adapter configurations, and training pipeline scripts are present and accounted for.
162: 
163: **Level 3 --- Full Build Verification**
164: 
165: Level 3 verification provides the highest level of assurance by attempting to compile, build, or reconstruct the deposited technology in a clean environment. In addition to all steps included in Level 1 and Level 2 verification, the Level 3 process includes:
166: 
167: > • Provisioning of a clean build or deployment environment based on the specifications set forth in the deposited documentation;
168: >
169: > • Attempt to compile and build the deposited source code using the deposited build scripts and instructions;
170: >
171: > • Attempt to load and instantiate deposited model weights using the deposited configuration files and code;
172: >
173: > • Execution of any deposited automated test suites or validation scripts;
174: >
175: > • Assessment of whether the deposited materials, taken as a whole, are sufficient to produce a functional instance of the deposited technology;
176: >
177: > • Documentation of any errors, failures, missing dependencies, or environmental issues encountered during the build process.
178: 
179: Level 3 verification is performed by Iron Mountain IPM\'s technical verification team, which includes engineers with experience in software development, DevOps, and machine-learning engineering. The scope, timeline, and cost of Level 3 verification are determined on a case-by-case basis depending on the complexity of the deposited technology and the requirements of the build or deployment process. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a detailed scope-of-work estimate prior to commencing Level 3 verification.
180: 
181: Upon completion of Level 3 verification, Iron Mountain IPM will provide a comprehensive written verification report documenting the verification methodology, the environment specifications, the results of each verification step, and any identified deficiencies or recommendations for improving the deposit.
182: 
183: **Verification Tier and Frequency.** The verification tier and the frequency of verification events shall be specified in the Escrow Agreement. Verification may be performed upon initial deposit, upon each updated deposit, annually, or on such other schedule as the parties may agree. The costs of verification services are borne by the requesting party (typically the Beneficiary) unless otherwise agreed in the Escrow Agreement.
184: 
185: **[VI. Release Conditions (Standard Triggers)]{.underline}**
186: 
187: The central purpose of the escrow arrangement is to ensure that the Beneficiary has access to the deposited technology assets in the event that specified release conditions occur. The Escrow Agent shall release a complete copy of the then-current deposit materials to the Beneficiary upon written certification by the Beneficiary, and subject to the dispute-resolution process described in Section VII below, that one or more of the following release conditions has occurred:
188: 
189: **1. Insolvency Event.** The Depositor files a voluntary petition for relief under any chapter of the United States Bankruptcy Code (Title 11, United States Code) or any analogous insolvency law of any jurisdiction; or an involuntary petition is filed against the Depositor under any such law and is not dismissed within sixty (60) days of filing; or the Depositor is the subject of proceedings for receivership, liquidation, dissolution, or winding up; or the Depositor makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; or the Depositor admits in writing its inability to pay its debts as they become due.
190: 
191: An insolvency event represents a fundamental threat to the Beneficiary\'s continued access to the deposited technology, as the Depositor\'s ability to provide ongoing support, maintenance, and development may be severely compromised or eliminated entirely. Release upon an insolvency event is intended to protect the Beneficiary\'s investment in the licensed technology and to ensure operational continuity.
192: 
193: **2. Material Uncured Breach.** The Depositor commits a material breach of the underlying Master Software License and Services Agreement or other vendor agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary, and such breach remains uncured for a period of sixty (60) calendar days following written notice from the Beneficiary to the Depositor specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail. If the underlying agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary specifies a different cure period for material breaches, the cure period specified in the underlying agreement shall govern for purposes of this release condition.
194: 
195: For the avoidance of doubt, the determination of whether a breach is \"material\" shall be made in accordance with the terms of the underlying agreement and applicable law. The Escrow Agent is not responsible for determining whether a material breach has in fact occurred; the Escrow Agent\'s sole obligation is to follow the notice and dispute-resolution procedures set forth in the Escrow Agreement.
196: 
197: **3. Cessation of Product Support.** The Depositor ceases to maintain or support the deposited technology, including by failing to provide updates, patches, bug fixes, or technical support in accordance with the terms of the underlying agreement; or the Depositor publicly announces the discontinuation, end-of-life, or sunsetting of the product line that includes the deposited technology; and in either case, the Depositor fails to provide a reasonable transition plan to the Beneficiary within sixty (60) calendar days following the Beneficiary\'s written request for such a plan. A \"reasonable transition plan\" shall, at minimum, include a timeline for transition, a description of the steps the Depositor will take to facilitate the Beneficiary\'s migration to an alternative solution or assumption of self-maintenance responsibilities, and cooperation with the Beneficiary\'s technical team during the transition period.
198: 
199: **4. Additional Triggers.** Any other release conditions mutually agreed upon in writing by the Depositor and the Beneficiary and expressly set forth in the Escrow Agreement or in a written amendment thereto executed by all three parties. The parties may, by way of example and not limitation, agree to include release conditions triggered by a change of control of the Depositor, the Depositor\'s failure to meet specified service-level commitments over a defined measurement period, or the Depositor\'s failure to deliver updated deposits within the timeframes specified in the Escrow Agreement.
200: 
201: **Scope of Release.** Upon the occurrence of a qualifying release event and the completion of the notice and dispute-resolution procedures set forth in Section VII below, the Escrow Agent shall deliver to the Beneficiary a complete copy of the then-current deposit materials held in escrow. The release of deposit materials to the Beneficiary does not transfer any ownership rights in the deposited materials; the Beneficiary\'s rights to use the released materials shall be governed by and limited to the terms of the underlying agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary, any applicable intellectual property licenses, and the terms of the Escrow Agreement.
202: 
203: **[VII. Dispute-Resolution Process for Contested Releases]{.underline}**
204: 
205: The Escrow Agreement will include a structured dispute-resolution process to protect the interests of both the Depositor and the Beneficiary in the event that a release request is contested. The standard dispute-resolution process operates as follows:
206: 
207: **A. Notice to Depositor.** Upon receipt of a written release request from the Beneficiary (together with the Beneficiary\'s written certification that one or more release conditions has occurred), the Escrow Agent shall provide written notice to the Depositor within five (5) business days of receipt of the release request. The notice shall include a copy of the Beneficiary\'s release request and certification and shall inform the Depositor of its right to object to the release within the timeframe specified below.
208: 
209: **B. Depositor\'s Right to Object.** The Depositor shall have thirty (30) calendar days from the date of receipt of the Escrow Agent\'s notice to deliver a written objection to the Escrow Agent. The written objection shall state the grounds for the objection in reasonable detail. The Depositor\'s objection shall be delivered to both the Escrow Agent and the Beneficiary.
210: 
211: **C. Effect of Objection.** If the Depositor timely delivers a written objection within the thirty (30) calendar day period, the deposit materials shall remain in escrow and shall not be released to the Beneficiary pending resolution of the dispute. The dispute may be resolved by any of the following means:
212: 
213: > \(a\) **Mutual Written Agreement.** The Depositor and the Beneficiary may resolve the dispute by mutual written agreement, which may include an agreement to release, an agreement not to release, or an agreement to release subject to specified conditions or limitations. Upon receipt of a mutual written agreement signed by both the Depositor and the Beneficiary directing the Escrow Agent to release or withhold the deposit materials, the Escrow Agent shall act in accordance with the instructions set forth in such agreement.
214: >
215: > \(b\) **Binding Arbitration.** Either the Depositor or the Beneficiary may initiate binding arbitration in accordance with the arbitration provisions set forth in the Escrow Agreement. Unless otherwise specified in the Escrow Agreement, arbitration shall be conducted under the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association by a single arbitrator with relevant technology industry experience, and the arbitration shall take place in Boston, Massachusetts, or such other location as the parties may agree. The Escrow Agent shall comply with any final, binding arbitration award directing the release or withholding of deposit materials.
216: >
217: > \(c\) **Final Court Order.** Either the Depositor or the Beneficiary may seek a final, non-appealable order from a court of competent jurisdiction directing the release or withholding of deposit materials. The Escrow Agent shall comply with any such order upon receipt of a certified copy thereof.
218: 
219: **D. Failure to Object.** If the Depositor does not deliver a written objection to the Escrow Agent within the thirty (30) calendar day period following receipt of the Escrow Agent\'s notice, the Escrow Agent shall release a complete copy of the then-current deposit materials to the Beneficiary as promptly as practicable, and in no event later than fifteen (15) business days following the expiration of the objection period.
220: 
221: **E. Escrow Agent\'s Role.** The Escrow Agent\'s role in the dispute-resolution process is strictly administrative. The Escrow Agent is not required to evaluate the merits of the Beneficiary\'s release request or the Depositor\'s objection, to determine whether a release condition has in fact occurred, or to mediate or adjudicate any dispute between the Depositor and the Beneficiary. The Escrow Agent shall be entitled to rely conclusively on the written certifications, objections, agreements, arbitration awards, and court orders received from the parties without independent investigation.
222: 
223: **[VIII. Annual Fees (Standard Schedule)]{.underline}**
224: 
225: The following fee schedule reflects Iron Mountain IPM\'s standard pricing for technology escrow services. Fees are quoted on an annual basis and are payable in advance upon execution of the Escrow Agreement and on each anniversary thereof throughout the term.
226: 
227:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
228:   **Service**                                       **Annual Fee**
229:   ------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------------
230:   Base escrow administration (single beneficiary)   \$2,500 -- \$5,000
231: 
232:   Additional beneficiary (each)                     \$1,000 -- \$2,000
233: 
234:   Level 1 verification (per event)                  \$1,500
235: 
236:   Level 2 verification (per event)                  \$3,500 -- \$7,500
237: 
238:   Level 3 verification (per event)                  \$10,000 -- \$25,000+ (scope-dependent)
239:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
240: 
241: **Fee Notes and Additional Terms:**
242: 
243: > • The base escrow administration fee covers the receipt, secure storage, and administrative management of deposit materials for one Depositor and one Beneficiary, including processing of up to four (4) routine deposit updates per year.
244: >
245: > • The range within each fee category reflects variability based on the size, complexity, and volume of the deposited materials, the specific requirements of the parties, and any negotiated terms.
246: >
247: > • Additional beneficiary fees apply for each beneficiary beyond the first that is added to the escrow arrangement. Each additional beneficiary is entitled to the same release rights and notice procedures as the initial Beneficiary.
248: >
249: > • Level 2 and Level 3 verification fees vary based on the size and complexity of the deposit, the number and type of technologies involved, and the scope of the verification engagement. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a fee estimate prior to commencing any Level 2 or Level 3 verification engagement.
250: >
251: > • Level 3 verification fees for complex deposits involving large-scale machine-learning models, multi-component software systems, or specialized hardware dependencies may exceed the standard range. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a detailed scope-of-work and fee proposal for any Level 3 engagement anticipated to exceed \$25,000.
252: >
253: > • Release processing fees, if any, will be specified in the Escrow Agreement.
254: 
255: All fees are subject to the then-current Iron Mountain IPM fee schedule in effect at the time of execution of the Escrow Agreement. Custom pricing is available for high-value or complex deposits, multi-agreement programs, and enterprise-scale escrow arrangements. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a formal fee proposal upon request.
256: 
257: The allocation of fees as between the Depositor and the Beneficiary shall be as agreed by the parties in the Escrow Agreement or, if not specified, as set forth in the underlying agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary.
258: 
259: **[IX. Limitation of Liability --- Escrow Agent]{.underline}**
260: 
261: Iron Mountain IPM\'s role under the Escrow Agreement is limited to that of an independent custodian and administrative agent. The Escrow Agreement will include the following limitation-of-liability provisions with respect to the Escrow Agent:
262: 
263: **Aggregate Liability Cap.** Iron Mountain IPM\'s total aggregate liability to the Depositor, the Beneficiary, and any other party arising out of or related to the Escrow Agreement, whether based in contract, tort, negligence, strict liability, or any other legal or equitable theory, shall not exceed the total fees actually paid to Iron Mountain IPM under the Escrow Agreement during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
264: 
265: **Exclusion of Consequential Damages.** In no event shall Iron Mountain IPM be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive, or exemplary damages, including without limitation damages for lost profits, lost revenue, lost data, business interruption, or loss of business opportunity, arising out of or related to the Escrow Agreement, regardless of whether such damages were foreseeable or whether Iron Mountain IPM was advised of the possibility of such damages.
266: 
267: **No Responsibility for Deposit Materials.** Iron Mountain IPM assumes no responsibility whatsoever for the completeness, accuracy, quality, functionality, fitness for a particular purpose, or merchantability of the deposited materials. Iron Mountain IPM does not represent or warrant that the deposited materials are sufficient to build, deploy, operate, or maintain the deposited technology, or that the deposited materials are free from defects, errors, viruses, or malicious code. Iron Mountain IPM\'s sole obligation with respect to the deposited materials is to securely store the materials as received from the Depositor and to release the materials in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement.
268: 
269: **Reliance on Instructions.** Iron Mountain IPM shall be entitled to act in reliance upon any written instruction, certification, notice, objection, agreement, arbitration award, or court order that it reasonably believes to be genuine and to have been signed or delivered by an authorized representative of the applicable party. Iron Mountain IPM shall have no liability for any action taken or omitted in good faith reliance upon such instructions.
270: 
271: The limitation-of-liability provisions set forth in this section are material to Iron Mountain IPM\'s willingness to serve as Escrow Agent and are reflected in the fee structure for the escrow services. The parties acknowledge that the fees charged by Iron Mountain IPM are set in consideration of these limitations and would be substantially higher in the absence of such limitations.
272: 
273: **[X. Contact]{.underline}**
274: 
275: For additional information regarding Iron Mountain IPM technology escrow services, to request a formal fee proposal, or to initiate the process of establishing a technology escrow arrangement, please contact:
276: 
277: > **Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc.** Account Services --- Technology Escrow
278: >
279: > Telephone: (800) 899-4766

281: > Email: ipm@ironmountain.com
282: >
283: > Web: www.ironmountain.com/services/intellectual-property-management
284: >
285: > Mailing Address:
286: >
287: > Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. One Federal Street Boston, MA 02110
288: 
289: Iron Mountain IPM account representatives are available to discuss escrow structure, verification requirements, fee proposals, and customization of escrow terms to meet the specific needs of the Depositor and Beneficiary.
290: 
291: *--- End of Key Terms Summary ---*
292:

TNS-VENDOR-2025-0043 and does not constitute a binding agreement, offer, or commitment by Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc., Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC, or TechNova Solutions, Inc. lines.text: **[IRON MOUNTAIN INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY MANAGEMENT, INC.]{.underline}**
**[Technology Escrow Agreement --- Key Terms Summary]{.underline}**
*Prepared for Internal Reference by TechNova Solutions, Inc.* *Internal Reference No. TNS-VENDOR-2025-0043*
*Date of Preparation: July 11, 2025*
**[I. Escrow Service Overview]{.underline}**

Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. (\"Iron Mountain IPM\" or \"Escrow Agent\") provides a standard three-party technology escrow service designed to safeguard the interests of licensees and customers of proprietary technology. The escrow arrangement ensures that critical technology assets --- including, without limitation, source code, machine-learning model weights, training data configurations, and related technical documentation --- are deposited with a neutral, independent escrow agent and held securely for the benefit of a designated beneficiary. In the event that specified release conditions occur, the deposited materials are made available to the beneficiary so that the beneficiary may continue to use, maintain, and operate the technology in accordance with the rights granted under the underlying license or vendor agreement.

The Iron Mountain IPM technology escrow service is widely recognized as an industry-standard mechanism for mitigating the risks associated with dependence on a single technology vendor. By requiring the vendor (the \"Depositor\") to place current and complete copies of the technology in escrow, the arrangement provides meaningful assurance to the licensee (the \"Beneficiary\") that it will retain the ability to access, maintain, and, where applicable, reconstruct the deposited technology in the event the Depositor is unable or unwilling to continue providing support, maintenance, or access to the technology.

**This summary is provided for reference and informational purposes only.** It is intended to facilitate internal review and evaluation by TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"TechNova\" or \"Beneficiary\") in connection with the proposed escrow arrangement involving Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"Meridian\" or \"Depositor\"). The governing terms of the escrow arrangement will be set forth exclusively in a fully executed Technology Escrow Agreement (the \"Escrow Agreement\") among the three parties --- Iron Mountain IPM, Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC, and TechNova Solutions, Inc. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between this summary and the executed Escrow Agreement, the terms of the executed Escrow Agreement shall control in all respects.
**[II. Parties]{.underline}**
The Technology Escrow Agreement contemplates the following three parties, each of which has distinct rights and obligations under the arrangement:

**Depositor (Vendor):** The owner or licensor of the deposited technology. The Depositor is responsible for delivering complete and current copies of all deposit materials to the Escrow Agent, maintaining and updating the deposit in accordance with the agreed-upon schedule, and cooperating with any verification processes specified in the Escrow Agreement. For purposes of this summary, the anticipated Depositor is:
> **Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC** A Delaware limited liability company

Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC is the owner and licensor of the proprietary cognitive analytics platform and associated machine-learning models licensed to TechNova Solutions, Inc. under the parties\' underlying Master Software License and Services Agreement. Meridian will be responsible for depositing and maintaining all specified technology assets in escrow in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement.

**Beneficiary (Customer):** The licensee or customer entitled to receive copies of the deposited materials upon the occurrence of a qualifying release event. The Beneficiary has the right to request release of the deposit materials, to request verification of the completeness and accuracy of the deposit, and to receive notice of certain events relating to the escrow arrangement. For purposes of this summary, the anticipated Beneficiary is:
> **TechNova Solutions, Inc.** A California corporation Internal Reference No.: TNS-VENDOR-2025-0043

TechNova Solutions, Inc. is the licensee of Meridian\'s proprietary technology and will be designated as the sole initial beneficiary under the Escrow Agreement. Additional beneficiaries may be added to the arrangement in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement and subject to the payment of applicable additional-beneficiary fees as set forth in Section VIII below.

**Escrow Agent:** The independent, neutral third party responsible for receiving, securely storing, and, upon the occurrence of specified release conditions or as otherwise directed, releasing the deposited materials. The Escrow Agent has no ownership interest in the deposited materials and acts solely in a custodial and administrative capacity. The Escrow Agent for this arrangement is:
> **Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc.** A subsidiary of Iron Mountain Incorporated

Iron Mountain IPM maintains secure, geographically redundant storage facilities and employs industry-standard security protocols to protect the confidentiality and integrity of all deposited materials throughout the term of the escrow arrangement. Iron Mountain IPM\'s obligations are limited to those expressly set forth in the Escrow Agreement, and Iron Mountain IPM does not assume any obligations under the underlying license or vendor agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary.
**[III. Deposit Materials]{.underline}**

The deposit scope encompasses the following categories of technology assets, as applicable to the deposited technology and as further specified in the deposit description schedule to be attached to the Escrow Agreement. The parties acknowledge that the completeness and utility of the deposit depend on the inclusion of all materials reasonably necessary for a qualified technical professional to understand, compile, build, deploy, and maintain the deposited technology.
The standard deposit scope includes:
**A. Source Code.** Complete and current source code for all modules, libraries, components, and build scripts comprising or required to build the deposited technology, including but not limited to:
> • All application source code files, organized in the same directory and project structure used by Depositor\'s development team;

> • All third-party libraries, frameworks, and dependencies included in or required by the build process, to the extent Depositor has the right to include such materials (or, where redistribution is not permitted, identification of all required third-party components together with version numbers and download or acquisition instructions);

> • All build scripts, makefiles, configuration files, and continuous-integration/continuous-deployment (CI/CD) pipeline definitions necessary to compile, link, and package the deposited technology into deployable form;
> • All automated test suites, test scripts, test data, and test harnesses included in the Depositor\'s standard development environment.
**B. Model Weights.** All machine-learning model weights associated with the deposited technology, including:
> • Base model weights for all foundational models used by the deposited technology;

> • Fine-tuned adapter weights (e.g., LoRA, QLoRA, or similar parameter-efficient fine-tuning artifacts) and any associated configuration files specifying adapter architecture, rank, and merging instructions;
> • Model checkpoint files for each production-release version of the deposited technology;
> • Tokenizer vocabularies, embedding matrices, and any custom model components necessary to load and execute the deposited models.

The specific model weights to be deposited shall be identified by mutual agreement of Depositor and Beneficiary and set forth in the deposit description schedule. Where the deposited technology incorporates third-party base models subject to separate license terms, the Depositor shall identify those models and provide copies of the applicable license terms to the extent necessary for the Beneficiary to understand the scope of rights available upon release.

**C. Training Data Configurations and Pipeline Artifacts.** All configurations, scripts, and artifacts necessary to understand and, where feasible, reproduce the training pipeline for the deposited models, including:
> • Hyperparameter specifications for each training run associated with a production-release model;
> • Data preprocessing scripts, data cleaning pipelines, and feature-engineering code;
> • Training configuration files (e.g., YAML, JSON, or TOML files specifying training parameters, optimizer settings, learning rate schedules, and data augmentation strategies);
> • Data pipeline orchestration scripts and workflow definitions;
> • Evaluation scripts, metrics definitions, and benchmark results for each deposited model version.

For the avoidance of doubt, the deposit of training data configurations and pipeline artifacts does not necessarily require the deposit of the underlying raw training data itself. The inclusion or exclusion of raw training data shall be determined by mutual agreement of Depositor and Beneficiary, taking into account data licensing restrictions, data volume, and the practical requirements for maintaining and retraining the deposited models. Where raw training data is not included, Depositor shall provide sufficient documentation to identify all training data sources, describe any licensing or access requirements, and enable the Beneficiary to obtain the necessary data independently.

**D. Technical Documentation.** Comprehensive technical documentation sufficient to enable a qualified technical professional to understand, build, deploy, configure, and maintain the deposited technology, including:
> • Build instructions providing step-by-step procedures for compiling, building, and packaging the deposited technology from source in a clean development environment;

> • Architecture diagrams depicting the high-level and component-level architecture of the deposited technology, including data flow diagrams, system integration points, and infrastructure requirements;

> • Deployment guides describing the procedures and requirements for deploying the deposited technology in production and non-production environments, including hardware and software prerequisites, environment configuration, and security settings;

> • Dependency manifests listing all third-party software components, libraries, frameworks, services, and tools required by the deposited technology, together with version numbers, license types, and acquisition instructions;
> • API documentation for all internal and external interfaces;
> • Database schemas, migration scripts, and data dictionary documentation;
> • Operations and maintenance guides, including monitoring, logging, backup, and disaster-recovery procedures.

**E. Additional Materials.** Any additional materials specified in the underlying Master Software License and Services Agreement or other vendor agreement between Depositor and Beneficiary, or as otherwise agreed in writing by the parties and set forth in the deposit description schedule attached to the Escrow Agreement. Such additional materials may include, by way of example and not limitation, encryption keys, digital certificates, hardware security module (HSM) configurations, container images, infrastructure-as-code templates, and environment-specific configuration files.

**Format Requirements.** All deposit materials shall be delivered in industry-standard, machine-readable formats agreed upon by the parties. Source code and scripts shall be delivered in their native file formats (e.g., .py, .java, .js, .go, .rs, .cpp, .h, .yaml, .json, .toml). Model weights shall be delivered in widely supported serialization formats (e.g., PyTorch .pt/.pth, TensorFlow SavedModel, ONNX, SafeTensors). Documentation shall be delivered in portable formats (e.g., PDF, Markdown, HTML). The Depositor shall include a top-level README file providing an index and description of all deposited materials.
**[IV. Deposit and Update Requirements]{.underline}**

Timely and regular deposits are essential to ensure that the escrowed materials remain current and useful in the event of a release. The Escrow Agreement will establish the following deposit and update obligations:

**A. Initial Deposit.** The Depositor shall deliver a complete initial deposit of all deposit materials described in Section III above to the Escrow Agent within thirty (30) calendar days following the date of full execution of the Escrow Agreement by all three parties. The initial deposit shall include all materials corresponding to the then-current production release version of the deposited technology as of the date of the Escrow Agreement.

The Depositor shall accompany each deposit (including the initial deposit) with a completed deposit description form, in the format prescribed by Iron Mountain IPM, identifying the materials included in the deposit, the version or release number of the deposited technology, the date of the deposit, and a manifest listing all files and directories included in the deposit together with file sizes and checksums (e.g., SHA-256 hashes) sufficient to verify file integrity.

**B. Update Frequency.** Following the initial deposit, the Depositor shall update the deposit materials on a regular and ongoing basis throughout the term of the Escrow Agreement. At a minimum, the Depositor shall deliver an updated deposit:
> • No less frequently than once per calendar quarter (i.e., at least four updates per calendar year); or

> • Within fifteen (15) business days following each major release, minor release, or material update to the deposited technology that is made available to the Beneficiary under the underlying agreement,

whichever results in more frequent updates. For purposes of this requirement, a \"material update\" includes any update that introduces new functionality, modifies the model architecture, retrains or fine-tunes model weights, changes the build or deployment process in a manner that would affect the Beneficiary\'s ability to build or deploy the technology, or addresses a critical security vulnerability.

Each updated deposit shall constitute a complete replacement of the prior deposit or, at the Depositor\'s option, a clearly documented incremental update together with instructions for integrating the incremental update with the prior deposit to produce a complete and current set of deposit materials.

**C. Deposit Media and Delivery Method.** All deposits shall be delivered via secure electronic transfer to Iron Mountain IPM\'s designated secure repository. Iron Mountain IPM will provide the Depositor with access credentials and transfer instructions upon execution of the Escrow Agreement. Electronic transfers shall be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and shall be encrypted at rest within Iron Mountain IPM\'s storage infrastructure.

Physical media deposits (e.g., encrypted USB drives, encrypted hard drives) will be accepted upon request, provided that the Depositor coordinates delivery logistics with Iron Mountain IPM in advance and that all physical media are encrypted using AES-256 or equivalent encryption, with decryption keys delivered separately to Iron Mountain IPM via a secure, out-of-band channel.

**D. Depositor Certifications.** With each deposit, the Depositor shall certify in writing that: (i) the deposited materials are complete and current as of the date of deposit; (ii) the deposited materials correspond to the version of the technology identified in the deposit description form; (iii) the Depositor has the right to deposit the materials with the Escrow Agent for the purposes contemplated by the Escrow Agreement; and (iv) the deposited materials, together with the accompanying documentation, are sufficient to enable a qualified technical professional to build, deploy, and maintain the deposited technology.
**[V. Verification Services]{.underline}**

Iron Mountain IPM offers optional technical verification services designed to confirm that the deposited materials are complete, readable, and, at the highest verification tier, operationally functional. Verification provides an important layer of assurance to the Beneficiary that the deposited materials will be useful and usable in the event of a release.
Iron Mountain IPM\'s verification services are available at three tiers, described below in order of increasing depth and rigor:
**Level 1 --- Inventory Verification**

Level 1 verification provides a baseline confirmation that the deposited files match the deposit description and manifest provided by the Depositor. The Level 1 verification process includes the following:
> • Comparison of the files and directories received against the file manifest and deposit description form submitted by the Depositor;
> • Confirmation that the number, names, and organization of deposited files are consistent with the manifest;
> • Verification of file integrity through checksum comparison (e.g., SHA-256 hash verification);
> • Identification of any discrepancies between the manifest and the actual deposit contents.

Upon completion of Level 1 verification, Iron Mountain IPM will provide a written verification report to both Depositor and Beneficiary identifying any discrepancies and confirming whether the deposit contents match the manifest. Level 1 verification does not include any assessment of file readability, format correctness, content completeness, or technical functionality.
**Level 2 --- Technical Review**
Level 2 verification provides a more thorough assessment of deposit completeness and readability. In addition to all steps included in Level 1 verification, the Level 2 process includes:
> • Confirmation that all deposited files can be opened and read using appropriate software tools;
> • Verification that deposited files are in the stated file formats and are not corrupted, truncated, or otherwise unreadable;
> • Review of the deposit for the presence of required build and deployment documentation, including build instructions, dependency manifests, and architecture documentation;
> • Assessment of overall deposit organization and completeness relative to the deposit description and the stated scope of the deposited technology;
> • Identification of any apparent gaps, missing components, or incomplete documentation.

Upon completion of Level 2 verification, Iron Mountain IPM will provide a detailed written verification report identifying the results of each verification step, including any identified gaps, deficiencies, or areas of concern. Level 2 verification does not include any attempt to compile, build, or execute the deposited technology.

**Iron Mountain IPM recommends Level 2 verification at minimum for deposits involving machine-learning model weights and training configurations.** Deposits of this nature are inherently complex and may involve large binary files, specialized serialization formats, and interdependencies among model components, training artifacts, and deployment infrastructure. Level 2 verification helps to ensure that the deposited materials are readable and organized in a manner that would be useful to the Beneficiary in the event of a release, and that critical components such as model weight files, adapter configurations, and training pipeline scripts are present and accounted for.
**Level 3 --- Full Build Verification**

Level 3 verification provides the highest level of assurance by attempting to compile, build, or reconstruct the deposited technology in a clean environment. In addition to all steps included in Level 1 and Level 2 verification, the Level 3 process includes:
> • Provisioning of a clean build or deployment environment based on the specifications set forth in the deposited documentation;
> • Attempt to compile and build the deposited source code using the deposited build scripts and instructions;
> • Attempt to load and instantiate deposited model weights using the deposited configuration files and code;
> • Execution of any deposited automated test suites or validation scripts;
> • Assessment of whether the deposited materials, taken as a whole, are sufficient to produce a functional instance of the deposited technology;
> • Documentation of any errors, failures, missing dependencies, or environmental issues encountered during the build process.

Level 3 verification is performed by Iron Mountain IPM\'s technical verification team, which includes engineers with experience in software development, DevOps, and machine-learning engineering. The scope, timeline, and cost of Level 3 verification are determined on a case-by-case basis depending on the complexity of the deposited technology and the requirements of the build or deployment process. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a detailed scope-of-work estimate prior to commencing Level 3 verification.

Upon completion of Level 3 verification, Iron Mountain IPM will provide a comprehensive written verification report documenting the verification methodology, the environment specifications, the results of each verification step, and any identified deficiencies or recommendations for improving the deposit.

**Verification Tier and Frequency.** The verification tier and the frequency of verification events shall be specified in the Escrow Agreement. Verification may be performed upon initial deposit, upon each updated deposit, annually, or on such other schedule as the parties may agree. The costs of verification services are borne by the requesting party (typically the Beneficiary) unless otherwise agreed in the Escrow Agreement.
**[VI. Release Conditions (Standard Triggers)]{.underline}**

The central purpose of the escrow arrangement is to ensure that the Beneficiary has access to the deposited technology assets in the event that specified release conditions occur. The Escrow Agent shall release a complete copy of the then-current deposit materials to the Beneficiary upon written certification by the Beneficiary, and subject to the dispute-resolution process described in Section VII below, that one or more of the following release conditions has occurred:

**1. Insolvency Event.** The Depositor files a voluntary petition for relief under any chapter of the United States Bankruptcy Code (Title 11, United States Code) or any analogous insolvency law of any jurisdiction; or an involuntary petition is filed against the Depositor under any such law and is not dismissed within sixty (60) days of filing; or the Depositor is the subject of proceedings for receivership, liquidation, dissolution, or winding up; or the Depositor makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; or the Depositor admits in writing its inability to pay its debts as they become due.

An insolvency event represents a fundamental threat to the Beneficiary\'s continued access to the deposited technology, as the Depositor\'s ability to provide ongoing support, maintenance, and development may be severely compromised or eliminated entirely. Release upon an insolvency event is intended to protect the Beneficiary\'s investment in the licensed technology and to ensure operational continuity.

**2. Material Uncured Breach.** The Depositor commits a material breach of the underlying Master Software License and Services Agreement or other vendor agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary, and such breach remains uncured for a period of sixty (60) calendar days following written notice from the Beneficiary to the Depositor specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail. If the underlying agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary specifies a different cure period for material breaches, the cure period specified in the underlying agreement shall govern for purposes of this release condition.

For the avoidance of doubt, the determination of whether a breach is \"material\" shall be made in accordance with the terms of the underlying agreement and applicable law. The Escrow Agent is not responsible for determining whether a material breach has in fact occurred; the Escrow Agent\'s sole obligation is to follow the notice and dispute-resolution procedures set forth in the Escrow Agreement.

**3. Cessation of Product Support.** The Depositor ceases to maintain or support the deposited technology, including by failing to provide updates, patches, bug fixes, or technical support in accordance with the terms of the underlying agreement; or the Depositor publicly announces the discontinuation, end-of-life, or sunsetting of the product line that includes the deposited technology; and in either case, the Depositor fails to provide a reasonable transition plan to the Beneficiary within sixty (60) calendar days following the Beneficiary\'s written request for such a plan. A \"reasonable transition plan\" shall, at minimum, include a timeline for transition, a description of the steps the Depositor will take to facilitate the Beneficiary\'s migration to an alternative solution or assumption of self-maintenance responsibilities, and cooperation with the Beneficiary\'s technical team during the transition period.

**4. Additional Triggers.** Any other release conditions mutually agreed upon in writing by the Depositor and the Beneficiary and expressly set forth in the Escrow Agreement or in a written amendment thereto executed by all three parties. The parties may, by way of example and not limitation, agree to include release conditions triggered by a change of control of the Depositor, the Depositor\'s failure to meet specified service-level commitments over a defined measurement period, or the Depositor\'s failure to deliver updated deposits within the timeframes specified in the Escrow Agreement.

**Scope of Release.** Upon the occurrence of a qualifying release event and the completion of the notice and dispute-resolution procedures set forth in Section VII below, the Escrow Agent shall deliver to the Beneficiary a complete copy of the then-current deposit materials held in escrow. The release of deposit materials to the Beneficiary does not transfer any ownership rights in the deposited materials; the Beneficiary\'s rights to use the released materials shall be governed by and limited to the terms of the underlying agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary, any applicable intellectual property licenses, and the terms of the Escrow Agreement.
**[VII. Dispute-Resolution Process for Contested Releases]{.underline}**

The Escrow Agreement will include a structured dispute-resolution process to protect the interests of both the Depositor and the Beneficiary in the event that a release request is contested. The standard dispute-resolution process operates as follows:

**A. Notice to Depositor.** Upon receipt of a written release request from the Beneficiary (together with the Beneficiary\'s written certification that one or more release conditions has occurred), the Escrow Agent shall provide written notice to the Depositor within five (5) business days of receipt of the release request. The notice shall include a copy of the Beneficiary\'s release request and certification and shall inform the Depositor of its right to object to the release within the timeframe specified below.

**B. Depositor\'s Right to Object.** The Depositor shall have thirty (30) calendar days from the date of receipt of the Escrow Agent\'s notice to deliver a written objection to the Escrow Agent. The written objection shall state the grounds for the objection in reasonable detail. The Depositor\'s objection shall be delivered to both the Escrow Agent and the Beneficiary.

**C. Effect of Objection.** If the Depositor timely delivers a written objection within the thirty (30) calendar day period, the deposit materials shall remain in escrow and shall not be released to the Beneficiary pending resolution of the dispute. The dispute may be resolved by any of the following means:

> \(a\) **Mutual Written Agreement.** The Depositor and the Beneficiary may resolve the dispute by mutual written agreement, which may include an agreement to release, an agreement not to release, or an agreement to release subject to specified conditions or limitations. Upon receipt of a mutual written agreement signed by both the Depositor and the Beneficiary directing the Escrow Agent to release or withhold the deposit materials, the Escrow Agent shall act in accordance with the instructions set forth in such agreement.

> \(b\) **Binding Arbitration.** Either the Depositor or the Beneficiary may initiate binding arbitration in accordance with the arbitration provisions set forth in the Escrow Agreement. Unless otherwise specified in the Escrow Agreement, arbitration shall be conducted under the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association by a single arbitrator with relevant technology industry experience, and the arbitration shall take place in Boston, Massachusetts, or such other location as the parties may agree. The Escrow Agent shall comply with any final, binding arbitration award directing the release or withholding of deposit materials.

> \(c\) **Final Court Order.** Either the Depositor or the Beneficiary may seek a final, non-appealable order from a court of competent jurisdiction directing the release or withholding of deposit materials. The Escrow Agent shall comply with any such order upon receipt of a certified copy thereof.

**D. Failure to Object.** If the Depositor does not deliver a written objection to the Escrow Agent within the thirty (30) calendar day period following receipt of the Escrow Agent\'s notice, the Escrow Agent shall release a complete copy of the then-current deposit materials to the Beneficiary as promptly as practicable, and in no event later than fifteen (15) business days following the expiration of the objection period.

**E. Escrow Agent\'s Role.** The Escrow Agent\'s role in the dispute-resolution process is strictly administrative. The Escrow Agent is not required to evaluate the merits of the Beneficiary\'s release request or the Depositor\'s objection, to determine whether a release condition has in fact occurred, or to mediate or adjudicate any dispute between the Depositor and the Beneficiary. The Escrow Agent shall be entitled to rely conclusively on the written certifications, objections, agreements, arbitration awards, and court orders received from the parties without independent investigation.
**[VIII. Annual Fees (Standard Schedule)]{.underline}**

The following fee schedule reflects Iron Mountain IPM\'s standard pricing for technology escrow services. Fees are quoted on an annual basis and are payable in advance upon execution of the Escrow Agreement and on each anniversary thereof throughout the term.
**Service**                                       **Annual Fee**
Base escrow administration (single beneficiary)   \$2,500 -- \$5,000
Additional beneficiary (each)                     \$1,000 -- \$2,000
Level 1 verification (per event)                  \$1,500
Level 2 verification (per event)                  \$3,500 -- \$7,500
Level 3 verification (per event)                  \$10,000 -- \$25,000+ (scope-dependent)
**Fee Notes and Additional Terms:**

> • The base escrow administration fee covers the receipt, secure storage, and administrative management of deposit materials for one Depositor and one Beneficiary, including processing of up to four (4) routine deposit updates per year.
> • The range within each fee category reflects variability based on the size, complexity, and volume of the deposited materials, the specific requirements of the parties, and any negotiated terms.

> • Additional beneficiary fees apply for each beneficiary beyond the first that is added to the escrow arrangement. Each additional beneficiary is entitled to the same release rights and notice procedures as the initial Beneficiary.

> • Level 2 and Level 3 verification fees vary based on the size and complexity of the deposit, the number and type of technologies involved, and the scope of the verification engagement. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a fee estimate prior to commencing any Level 2 or Level 3 verification engagement.

> • Level 3 verification fees for complex deposits involving large-scale machine-learning models, multi-component software systems, or specialized hardware dependencies may exceed the standard range. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a detailed scope-of-work and fee proposal for any Level 3 engagement anticipated to exceed \$25,000.
> • Release processing fees, if any, will be specified in the Escrow Agreement.

All fees are subject to the then-current Iron Mountain IPM fee schedule in effect at the time of execution of the Escrow Agreement. Custom pricing is available for high-value or complex deposits, multi-agreement programs, and enterprise-scale escrow arrangements. Iron Mountain IPM will provide a formal fee proposal upon request.

The allocation of fees as between the Depositor and the Beneficiary shall be as agreed by the parties in the Escrow Agreement or, if not specified, as set forth in the underlying agreement between the Depositor and the Beneficiary.
**[IX. Limitation of Liability --- Escrow Agent]{.underline}**

Iron Mountain IPM\'s role under the Escrow Agreement is limited to that of an independent custodian and administrative agent. The Escrow Agreement will include the following limitation-of-liability provisions with respect to the Escrow Agent:

**Aggregate Liability Cap.** Iron Mountain IPM\'s total aggregate liability to the Depositor, the Beneficiary, and any other party arising out of or related to the Escrow Agreement, whether based in contract, tort, negligence, strict liability, or any other legal or equitable theory, shall not exceed the total fees actually paid to Iron Mountain IPM under the Escrow Agreement during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

**Exclusion of Consequential Damages.** In no event shall Iron Mountain IPM be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive, or exemplary damages, including without limitation damages for lost profits, lost revenue, lost data, business interruption, or loss of business opportunity, arising out of or related to the Escrow Agreement, regardless of whether such damages were foreseeable or whether Iron Mountain IPM was advised of the possibility of such damages.

**No Responsibility for Deposit Materials.** Iron Mountain IPM assumes no responsibility whatsoever for the completeness, accuracy, quality, functionality, fitness for a particular purpose, or merchantability of the deposited materials. Iron Mountain IPM does not represent or warrant that the deposited materials are sufficient to build, deploy, operate, or maintain the deposited technology, or that the deposited materials are free from defects, errors, viruses, or malicious code. Iron Mountain IPM\'s sole obligation with respect to the deposited materials is to securely store the materials as received from the Depositor and to release the materials in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement.

**Reliance on Instructions.** Iron Mountain IPM shall be entitled to act in reliance upon any written instruction, certification, notice, objection, agreement, arbitration award, or court order that it reasonably believes to be genuine and to have been signed or delivered by an authorized representative of the applicable party. Iron Mountain IPM shall have no liability for any action taken or omitted in good faith reliance upon such instructions.

The limitation-of-liability provisions set forth in this section are material to Iron Mountain IPM\'s willingness to serve as Escrow Agent and are reflected in the fee structure for the escrow services. The parties acknowledge that the fees charged by Iron Mountain IPM are set in consideration of these limitations and would be substantially higher in the absence of such limitations.
**[X. Contact]{.underline}**

For additional information regarding Iron Mountain IPM technology escrow services, to request a formal fee proposal, or to initiate the process of establishing a technology escrow arrangement, please contact:
> **Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc.** Account Services --- Technology Escrow
> Email: ipm@ironmountain.com
> Web: www.ironmountain.com/services/intellectual-property-management
> Mailing Address:
> Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. One Federal Street Boston, MA 02110

Iron Mountain IPM account representatives are available to discuss escrow structure, verification requirements, fee proposals, and customization of escrow terms to meet the specific needs of the Depositor and Beneficiary.
*--- End of Key Terms Summary ---*

**NOTICE:** This summary is provided for informational and reference purposes only in connection with TechNova Solutions, Inc. internal reference no. TNS-VENDOR-2025-0043 and does not constitute a binding agreement, offer, or commitment by Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc., Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC, or TechNova Solutions, Inc. Binding terms shall be governed exclusively by the executed Technology Escrow Agreement among the parties. This summary is confidential and intended solely for the internal use of TechNova Solutions, Inc. and its authorized advisors in evaluating the proposed escrow arrangement. Distribution of this summary to third parties without the prior written consent of Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. is prohibited.
