**A.1 Purpose**

This Exhibit A describes the Technical and Organizational Measures (\"TOMs\") implemented and maintained by Vendor to protect Personal Information against unauthorized or unlawful Processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, alteration, or disclosure. These measures are referenced in Article 5 of the DPA and form an integral part thereof. Vendor shall implement and maintain these measures throughout the term of the DPA and shall update them as necessary to address evolving threats, vulnerabilities, and industry best practices.
**A.2 Organizational Security Measures**
Vendor shall implement and maintain the following organizational security measures:

> \(a\) **Information Security Governance.** Vendor shall maintain a formal information security governance structure, including a designated Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or equivalent security officer with responsibility for the development, implementation, oversight, and enforcement of Vendor\'s information security program. The security officer shall report to Vendor\'s senior management on a regular basis regarding the status of the information security program.

> \(b\) **Security Awareness Training.** Vendor shall provide regular security awareness training to all personnel who have access to Personal Information, including employees, contractors, and temporary staff. Training shall be provided upon onboarding and at least annually thereafter, and shall cover topics including data handling procedures, phishing awareness, password security, incident reporting, and Vendor\'s obligations under this DPA and Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall maintain records of training completion.

> \(c\) **Background Checks.** Vendor shall conduct background checks on all personnel who will have access to Personal Information, to the extent permitted by Applicable Data Protection Laws and consistent with the sensitivity of the Personal Information to be accessed. Background checks shall be conducted prior to granting access and shall be appropriate to the role and level of access.

> \(d\) **Information Security Policies and Procedures.** Vendor shall maintain documented information security policies and procedures that address, at a minimum, data classification, access control, incident response, acceptable use, data retention and destruction, change management, and third-party risk management. Policies and procedures shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, and more frequently as needed to address changes in Vendor\'s operations, threats, or Applicable Data Protection Laws.
**A.3 Technical Security Measures**
Vendor shall implement and maintain the following technical security measures:

> \(a\) **Encryption Standards.** All Personal Information stored by Vendor shall be encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption or an equivalent or stronger standard. All Personal Information transmitted by Vendor shall be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher. Encryption key management practices shall follow industry best practices, including secure key generation, storage, rotation, and destruction.

> \(b\) **Access Control.** Vendor shall implement and maintain role-based access controls (RBAC) based on the principle of least privilege, ensuring that each user is granted only the minimum level of access necessary to perform their assigned duties. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) shall be required for all access to systems Processing Personal Information, including remote access and administrative access. Access rights shall be reviewed at least quarterly and promptly revoked upon personnel termination, role change, or when access is no longer required.

> \(c\) **Network Security.** Vendor shall implement and maintain firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS), and network segmentation to isolate systems Processing Personal Information from other systems and networks. Vendor shall monitor network traffic for anomalies and unauthorized activity on a continuous basis.

> \(d\) **Endpoint Protection.** Vendor shall deploy and maintain anti-malware software, endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions, and host-based firewalls on all endpoints that access or Process Personal Information. Vendor shall ensure that all endpoint protection solutions are updated with current signatures and patches.

> \(e\) **Logging and Monitoring.** Vendor shall implement centralized log management and security event monitoring for all systems that Process Personal Information. Logs shall record, at a minimum, user authentication events, data access events, data modification events, data deletion events, and administrative actions. Logs shall be retained for a minimum of \[**\_\_\_**\] and shall be protected against unauthorized access, modification, or deletion. Vendor shall conduct regular review and analysis of logs to identify and respond to potential security incidents.

> \(f\) **Vulnerability Management.** Vendor shall conduct regular vulnerability scanning of its systems and infrastructure, no less frequently than quarterly, and shall conduct annual penetration testing by a qualified independent third party. Vendor shall implement a patch management program to ensure timely remediation of identified vulnerabilities, with critical and high-severity vulnerabilities remediated within the timeframes established by Vendor\'s vulnerability management policy (and in no event later than thirty (30) days of identification for critical vulnerabilities and sixty (60) days for high-severity vulnerabilities).

> \(g\) **Data Loss Prevention.** Vendor shall implement data loss prevention (DLP) measures to monitor, detect, and prevent unauthorized exfiltration or leakage of Personal Information, including DLP controls at the network, endpoint, and application layers.
**A.4 Physical Security Measures**
Vendor shall implement and maintain the following physical security measures:

> \(a\) **Physical Access Controls.** Vendor shall restrict physical access to data centers, server rooms, and other facilities where Personal Information is stored or Processed. Physical access shall be controlled through measures such as badge access systems, biometric authentication, security guards, and visitor escort policies.

> \(b\) **Environmental Controls.** Vendor\'s data centers and facilities shall be equipped with environmental controls, including fire detection and suppression systems, climate control (temperature and humidity monitoring), uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), backup power generators, and water damage detection systems.

> \(c\) **Visitor Access Policies.** Vendor shall maintain visitor access policies that require all visitors to data centers and facilities to sign in, present valid identification, be accompanied by authorized personnel at all times, and sign out upon departure. Visitor logs shall be maintained for a minimum of twelve (12) months.
**A.5 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery**
Vendor shall implement and maintain the following business continuity and disaster recovery measures:

> \(a\) **Business Continuity Plan (BCP) and Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP).** Vendor shall maintain documented business continuity and disaster recovery plans that address the restoration of systems and data in the event of a disruption or disaster. BCPs and DRPs shall be tested at least annually through tabletop exercises, simulations, or live failover tests, and updated based on test results and changes to Vendor\'s operating environment.

> \(b\) **Backup Procedures.** Vendor shall maintain regular backup procedures for all Personal Information, with backups performed at a frequency appropriate to the criticality of the data. Backups shall be encrypted and stored in geographically separate locations from the primary data. Recovery time objectives (RTO): \[**\_\_\_**\]. Recovery point objectives (RPO): \[**\_\_\_**\].

> \(b\) Trust services criteria covered by the report include: Security, Availability, and Confidentiality.

**C.8 Processing Location(s)**
Personal Information shall be Processed at the following locations:
> • \[**\_\_\_**\] *(e.g., Vendor\'s primary data center located in \[city, state\])*
> • \[**\_\_\_**\] *(e.g., Vendor\'s disaster recovery site located in \[city, state\])*

**C.9 Applicable Data Protection Laws**
The following Data Protection Laws are applicable to the Processing of Personal Information under this DPA:

> • Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314)

349: > \(c\) **Cessation of Support or End-of-Life.** The vendor ceases product support for the applicable platform or product, announces an end-of-life date for the applicable platform or product, or otherwise discontinues the services provided to TechNova under the agreement.
350: 
351: Release must be automatic upon verification of the trigger event by the escrow agent. The escrow agent must be authorized under the escrow agreement to verify the occurrence of the trigger event based on documentation provided by TechNova (e.g., copies of bankruptcy filings, written breach notices, vendor end-of-life announcements) and to release the escrow materials to TechNova without requiring the vendor\'s consent, approval, or cooperation.
352: 
353: **7.5 --- Negotiation Guidance**
354: 
355: Negotiating attorneys should propose Iron Mountain IPM as the escrow agent in every initial draft. If the vendor insists on an alternative escrow agent, accept only a Tier 1 provider with verifiable AI/ML escrow capabilities. Do not accept a general-purpose escrow agent that lacks specific experience with AI/ML model artifacts, as such agents may not have the technical infrastructure or processes necessary to handle large model files, verify deposit completeness, or support the quarterly update cadence required by this Playbook.
356: 
357: The sixty-day cure period for the material breach release trigger is the TechNova standard. Negotiating attorneys should not agree to extend this period beyond sixty (60) days without the written approval of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions. An extension to ninety (90) days may be acceptable in limited circumstances (e.g., where the nature of the breach reasonably requires additional time to cure), but any extension beyond ninety (90) days is a Red-zone concession.
358: 
359: **[Section 8 --- Insurance Requirements]{.underline}**
360: 
361: **8.1 --- Commercial General Liability (CGL)**
362: 
363: Every AI/ML vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with minimum limits of five million dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence and ten million dollars (\$10,000,000) in the aggregate. This coverage must be maintained throughout the term of the agreement and for a period of at least two (2) years following the expiration or termination of the agreement.
364: 
365: This requirement is standard and non-negotiable. TechNova must be named as an additional insured on the vendor\'s CGL policy. The vendor must provide TechNova with a certificate of insurance evidencing the required coverage prior to the execution of the agreement and annually thereafter during the term.
366: 
367: **8.2 --- Technology Errors & Omissions (Tech E&O)**
368: 
369: **Green (Preferred).** For any AI/ML vendor engagement with a TCV exceeding \$5,000,000, TechNova\'s preferred position is that the vendor maintain technology errors and omissions insurance with a minimum limit of ten million dollars (\$10,000,000) per occurrence. This elevated requirement reflects the heightened risk associated with large-scale AI/ML deployments and the potential magnitude of losses arising from model errors, platform failures, or other technology-related claims.
370: 
371: **Yellow (Acceptable / Minimum).** For all AI/ML vendor engagements (regardless of TCV), the minimum acceptable Tech E&O coverage is five million dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence. This is the absolute floor for Tech E&O coverage.
372: 
373: **Red (Walk-Away).** Any Tech E&O coverage below \$5,000,000 per occurrence is a walk-away. Acceptance of a Tech E&O limit below \$5,000,000 requires VP Legal approval with a documented risk assessment.
374: 
375: For engagements with a TCV exceeding \$5,000,000, negotiating attorneys should push firmly for the \$10,000,000 preferred limit. If the vendor\'s current policy limit is \$5,000,000, explore whether the vendor is willing to obtain an endorsement, policy amendment, or increased limits as a condition of the agreement. The cost of increased coverage should be borne by the vendor and should not be passed through to TechNova. If the vendor demonstrates that \$10,000,000 in Tech E&O coverage is not commercially available or is prohibitively expensive, the negotiating attorney should escalate to the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions with a written risk assessment before accepting the \$5,000,000 minimum.
376: 
377: **8.3 --- Umbrella / Excess Liability**
378: 
379: Every AI/ML vendor must maintain umbrella or excess liability insurance with a minimum limit of ten million dollars (\$10,000,000). This coverage must sit excess of the vendor\'s CGL and Tech E&O policies and must provide coverage for claims that exceed the underlying policy limits.
380: 
381: This requirement is standard and non-negotiable.
382: 
383: **8.4 --- Negotiation Guidance**
384: 
385: Insurance requirements should be included in the initial draft of every AI/ML vendor agreement, typically as a schedule or exhibit setting forth the required coverage types and minimum limits. Insurance provisions are generally not traded for concessions in other areas of the negotiation, as they serve a fundamentally different risk-management function than the other commercial and legal terms of the agreement.
386: 
387: If a vendor resists the \$10,000,000 Tech E&O requirement for a high-TCV deal, the negotiating attorney should escalate to the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions with a risk assessment that considers: (a) the TCV and duration of the engagement; (b) the nature of the vendor\'s services and the potential magnitude of technology-related claims; (c) the vendor\'s financial condition and balance sheet strength; and (d) the availability of other contractual protections (e.g., liability caps, indemnification, escrow) that may partially mitigate the risk. Only after this assessment should a decision be made to accept the \$5,000,000 minimum.
388: 
389: Negotiating attorneys should also confirm that the vendor\'s insurance policies do not contain exclusions that would effectively negate coverage for the types of claims most likely to arise in an AI/ML vendor relationship, such as exclusions for AI-generated output claims, data breach claims, or intellectual property infringement claims.
390: 
391: **[Section 9 --- AI-Output Risk Allocation]{.underline}**
392: 
393: **9.1 --- Scope**
394: 
395: This section applies to any AI/ML vendor engagement where the vendor\'s model or platform generates outputs --- including text, predictions, scores, classifications, recommendations, images, code, or any other generated content --- that are used in TechNova\'s customer-facing products or services (e.g., the LendStream platform), or that inform decisions affecting consumers (e.g., credit decisions, risk assessments, customer communications). As AI-generated outputs play an increasingly central role in TechNova\'s product offerings, it is essential that the risk of third-party claims arising from those outputs be appropriately allocated between TechNova and its AI/ML vendors.
396: 
397: **9.2 --- Preferred Position (Green)**
398: 
399: TechNova\'s preferred position is that the vendor provides a full indemnity to TechNova for third-party claims related to AI-generated outputs. Specifically, the vendor\'s indemnity must cover:
400: 
401: > \(a\) **IP Infringement Claims.** Third-party claims alleging that AI-generated outputs infringe, misappropriate, or otherwise violate any intellectual property rights, including patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, and rights of publicity.
402: >
403: > \(b\) **Regulatory and Legal Claims.** Third-party claims alleging that AI-generated outputs violate applicable law, including but not limited to consumer protection statutes, fair lending laws (including the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and the Fair Housing Act), financial services regulations, unfair or deceptive acts or practices (UDAP/UDAAP) prohibitions, and any other federal, state, or local law or regulation applicable to the use of AI-generated outputs in TechNova\'s business.
404: 
405: The indemnity must cover TechNova\'s authorized use of the outputs in accordance with the terms of the agreement and the vendor\'s published documentation and usage guidelines. The vendor may not condition the indemnity on TechNova\'s use of the outputs in a specific manner beyond what is set forth in the agreement and the vendor\'s documentation.
406: 
407: This Green-tier position should be proposed in every initial draft of an AI/ML vendor agreement.
408: 
409: **9.3 --- Acceptable Fallback (Yellow)**
410: 
411: If the vendor will not provide a full output indemnity, TechNova will accept a shared-risk framework structured as follows:
412: 
413: **Vendor First-Dollar Coverage.** The vendor provides first-dollar coverage for defense costs (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) and settlements or judgments arising from third-party claims related to AI-generated outputs, up to the applicable liability cap or super-cap negotiated under Section 5. This means the vendor bears the initial financial exposure for output-related claims, and TechNova is not required to contribute to defense costs or settlements until the vendor\'s coverage tier is exhausted.
414: 
415: **Residual Risk.** TechNova bears the residual risk above the vendor\'s coverage tier. The parties may negotiate the allocation of residual risk above the vendor\'s cap, but the vendor must bear the first-dollar exposure as described above.
416: 
417: **Vendor Obligations.** The shared-risk framework must include the following vendor obligations:
418: 
419: > \(a\) **Cooperation in Defense.** The vendor must cooperate fully with TechNova in the defense of any third-party claim related to AI-generated outputs, including providing access to relevant technical documentation, model architecture information, training data provenance records, and vendor personnel with knowledge of the model\'s design and operation.
420: >
421: > \(b\) **Prompt Remediation.** Upon TechNova\'s notice that an AI-generated output has given rise to a third-party claim or a credible threat of a third-party claim, the vendor must implement prompt remediation measures, which may include retraining the model, adjusting output filters, modifying the inference pipeline, or implementing other technical measures to prevent recurrence of the offending output.
422: 
423: **9.4 --- Carve-Outs**
424: 
425: The vendor\'s AI-output indemnity obligation (whether structured as a full indemnity under Section 9.2 or as a shared-risk framework under Section 9.3) may exclude the following categories of claims:
426: 
427: > \(a\) **Post-Receipt Modification.** Claims caused by TechNova\'s modification of AI-generated outputs after receipt from the vendor\'s platform. For example, if TechNova receives a model prediction from the vendor\'s API and then alters, reformats, or recontextualizes the prediction before presenting it to a consumer, and the claim arises from TechNova\'s modification rather than from the vendor\'s original output, the vendor\'s indemnity obligation does not apply.
428: >
429: > \(b\) **Unauthorized Use.** Claims arising from TechNova\'s use of outputs outside the documented use case or in a manner inconsistent with the vendor\'s published usage guidelines. For example, if the vendor\'s usage guidelines expressly prohibit the use of a particular model for credit decisioning, and TechNova uses the model for credit decisioning notwithstanding that prohibition, the vendor\'s indemnity obligation does not apply to claims arising from that unauthorized use.
430: 
431: No other carve-outs to the vendor\'s AI-output indemnity obligation are acceptable without the express approval of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions. In particular, negotiating attorneys should be alert to vendor proposals that attempt to carve out liability for \"model hallucinations,\" \"accuracy limitations,\" or \"inherent limitations of AI technology.\" Such carve-outs are overbroad and would effectively eliminate the vendor\'s indemnity obligation for the most common categories of AI-output claims.
432: 
433: **9.5 --- Negotiation Guidance**
434: 
435: AI-output risk allocation is a relatively novel provision in AI/ML vendor agreements, and many vendors will not have standard language addressing this issue. Negotiating attorneys should be prepared to propose TechNova\'s preferred position (Section 9.2) in the initial draft and to educate vendor counsel on the rationale for the provision. The key points to communicate are:
436: 
437: > • TechNova is deploying the vendor\'s model in customer-facing products and services, and the outputs generated by the model directly impact TechNova\'s customers.
438: >
439: > • If the vendor\'s model generates an output that infringes a third party\'s intellectual property rights or violates applicable law, TechNova will be the party sued --- and TechNova needs the vendor to stand behind its product.
440: >
441: > • The vendor is best positioned to control the risk associated with its model\'s outputs because the vendor designed, trained, and maintains the model.
442: 
443: If the vendor has not previously addressed AI-output risk allocation in its standard terms, the shared-risk framework described in Section 9.3 is an acceptable landing zone and should be presented as a reasonable compromise. Emphasize that the shared-risk framework limits the vendor\'s exposure to the applicable liability cap or super-cap, which already constrains the vendor\'s total financial exposure.
444: 
445: Negotiating attorneys should coordinate with Product Engineering to document the specific use cases and output types that will be covered by the AI-output indemnity. A clear and specific description of \"authorized use\" will strengthen TechNova\'s position in any future claim and will provide the vendor with reasonable certainty about the scope of its obligation.
446: 
447: Any vendor that categorically refuses both the full indemnity (Section 9.2) and the shared-risk framework (Section 9.3) --- that is, any vendor that takes the position that it has no responsibility whatsoever for claims arising from its model\'s outputs --- should be flagged for escalation to the VP Legal. Categorical refusal to accept any form of AI-output risk allocation is a Red-zone position.
448: 
449: **[Section 10 --- Governing Law & Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**
450: 
451: **10.1 --- Governing Law**
452: 
453: **Green (Preferred / Strong Preference).** TechNova\'s strong preference is that all AI/ML vendor agreements be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Delaware law provides a well-developed, predictable, and commercially sophisticated body of contract law, and TechNova\'s corporate governance structure is organized under Delaware law. This preference should be reflected in every initial draft.
454: 
455: **Yellow (Acceptable Alternatives).** If the vendor will not agree to Delaware governing law, TechNova will accept either of the following alternatives:
456: 
457: > • **New York law**, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. New York has a similarly well-developed body of commercial contract law and is widely accepted as a governing law choice for technology transactions.
458: >
459: > • **Texas law**, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. TechNova\'s principal offices are located in Austin, Texas, and Texas law is an appropriate alternative governing law choice for engagements with Texas-based vendors or where the services will be primarily performed in Texas.
460: 
461: Either of these alternatives falls within the Yellow zone and may be accepted by the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions without further escalation.
462: 
463: **Red (Walk-Away).** Any governing law other than Delaware, New York, or Texas is a walk-away absent VP Legal approval. This includes, without limitation, the vendor\'s home-state law (unless the vendor is domiciled in Delaware, New York, or Texas), foreign law, or any other jurisdiction that does not provide the predictability and sophistication of Delaware, New York, or Texas commercial contract law.
464: 
465: **10.2 --- Forum / Dispute Resolution**
466: 
467: **Preferred.** TechNova\'s preferred dispute resolution forum is exclusive jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery, or, if the Court of Chancery declines jurisdiction (e.g., because the dispute involves a claim for money damages that is not ancillary to equitable relief), the United States District Court for the District of Delaware. The Delaware Court of Chancery provides expedited proceedings, experienced judges with expertise in commercial disputes, and well-developed procedural rules for complex business litigation.
468: 
469: **Acceptable Alternative.** If the vendor will not agree to a Delaware forum, TechNova will accept exclusive jurisdiction in the federal or state courts located in one of the following jurisdictions, consistent with the governing law selected:
470: 
471: > • **New York:** The United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, or the Commercial Division of the New York Supreme Court, New York County.
472: >
473: > • **Texas:** The United States District Court for the Western District of Texas, Austin Division, or the state courts of Travis County, Texas.
474: 
475: **Avoid: Mandatory Binding Arbitration.** TechNova\'s strong preference is to avoid mandatory binding arbitration for any dispute, and particularly for disputes with an amount in controversy exceeding \$1,000,000. Mandatory arbitration limits TechNova\'s discovery rights, eliminates the right to appeal, and may result in an unreasoned award that does not provide adequate guidance for the parties\' ongoing relationship.
476: 
477: If the vendor insists on mandatory arbitration, the negotiating attorney should pursue the following alternatives in order of preference:
478: 
479: > \(a\) **Litigation Carve-Out.** Negotiate a carve-out providing that disputes with an amount in controversy exceeding \$1,000,000 shall be resolved by litigation in the agreed forum (Delaware, New York, or Texas courts), with arbitration applicable only to disputes below the \$1,000,000 threshold.
480: >
481: > \(b\) **Enhanced Arbitration.** If a litigation carve-out is not achievable, negotiate enhanced arbitration terms that provide TechNova with protections approximating those available in litigation, including at minimum: (i) a three-arbitrator panel; (ii) arbitration administered under the American Arbitration Association (\"AAA\") Commercial Rules; (iii) full discovery rights, including document production and depositions; and (iv) a reasoned written award setting forth the arbitrators\' findings of fact and conclusions of law.
482: 
483: **10.3 --- Negotiation Guidance**
484: 
485: Open with Delaware law and a Delaware forum in every initial draft. If the vendor proposes its home-state law or mandatory arbitration, counter with Delaware and flag the issue for the negotiating team.
486: 
487: Do not concede to mandatory arbitration for high-value disputes without first exploring the litigation carve-out described in Section 10.2(a). If arbitration is ultimately unavoidable, insist on the enhanced arbitration terms described in Section 10.2(b). Under no circumstances should TechNova agree to arbitration before a single arbitrator, arbitration without discovery rights, or arbitration resulting in an unreasoned award.
488: 
489: If the vendor is domiciled in a jurisdiction other than Delaware, New York, or Texas, the vendor will likely push for its home-state law and forum. In such cases, the negotiating attorney should explain TechNova\'s strong preference for a neutral, commercially sophisticated jurisdiction and propose Delaware as a true neutral forum. If the vendor resists Delaware, explore New York or Texas as alternatives. If the vendor will not agree to any of the three approved jurisdictions, escalate to the VP Legal before accepting an alternative.
490: 
491: **[Section 11 --- Indemnification]{.underline}**
492: 
493: **11.1 --- Scope of IP Indemnity**
494: 
495: **Green (Preferred) / Minimum (Non-Negotiable).** The vendor\'s intellectual property indemnity must cover all forms of intellectual property rights, without limitation. Specifically, the indemnity must cover claims alleging infringement, misappropriation, or violation of:
496: 
497: > \(a\) **Patents** --- including utility patents, design patents, and provisional patent rights, whether registered or unregistered, and whether issued in the United States or in any foreign jurisdiction.
498: >
499: > \(b\) **Copyrights** --- including rights in original works of authorship, derivative works, compilations, and databases, whether registered or unregistered.
500: >
501: > \(c\) **Trade Secrets** --- including rights in proprietary algorithms, methodologies, techniques, processes, and know-how, whether or not the information qualifies as a \"trade secret\" under the Defend Trade Secrets Act or applicable state uniform trade secrets acts.
502: >
503: > \(d\) **Trademarks** --- including rights in registered and unregistered trademarks, service marks, trade names, and trade dress.
504: >
505: > \(e\) **Rights of Publicity and Moral Rights** --- to the extent applicable under the law of any relevant jurisdiction, including claims alleging unauthorized use of a person\'s name, likeness, or identity in AI-generated outputs.
506: 
507: The indemnity must not be limited to registered United States patents and copyrights. Many vendor form agreements contain IP indemnity provisions that are narrowly scoped to cover only \"infringement of a valid, issued U.S. patent or registered U.S. copyright.\" This narrow scope is insufficient for TechNova\'s purposes, as it would leave TechNova without indemnification coverage for trade secret misappropriation claims (which are increasingly common in the AI/ML space), trademark infringement claims, foreign IP claims, and claims based on unregistered copyrights. Any vendor draft that narrows the indemnity to only registered U.S. patents and copyrights must be revised to cover all intellectual property rights as described above.
508: 
509: The indemnity must cover TechNova\'s authorized use of the vendor\'s platform, models, and outputs in accordance with the agreement. The indemnity should not be conditioned on TechNova\'s use of the vendor\'s platform in an unmodified form or on TechNova\'s exclusive use of the vendor\'s recommended configuration, provided that TechNova\'s use is within the scope of the authorized use described in the agreement.
510: 
511: **11.2 --- Standard Indemnity Obligations**
512: 
513: **Vendor\'s Indemnification of TechNova.** The vendor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless TechNova and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all third-party claims, losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or relating to:
514: 
515: > \(a\) Infringement or misappropriation of any intellectual property right by the vendor\'s platform, models, outputs, or any component thereof, when used by TechNova as authorized under the agreement.
516: >
517: > \(b\) The vendor\'s breach of its data processing and privacy obligations as set forth in the agreement and the applicable DPA (see Section 4), including any breach resulting in unauthorized access to, disclosure of, or loss of TechNova customer data.
518: >
519: > \(c\) The vendor\'s violation of applicable law in the performance of the agreement, including violations of consumer protection, fair lending, financial services, and data privacy laws and regulations.
520: 
521: **TechNova\'s Indemnification of Vendor.** TechNova will indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the vendor and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all third-party claims, losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or relating to:
522: 
523: > \(a\) TechNova\'s breach of the agreement, including any breach of TechNova\'s representations, warranties, or covenants.
524: >
525: > \(b\) TechNova\'s use of the vendor\'s platform or outputs in a manner that is not authorized by the agreement or that is inconsistent with the vendor\'s published documentation and usage guidelines.
526: 
527: **11.3 --- Indemnity Procedures**
528: 
529: The agreement must include standard indemnification procedures, including the following:
530: 
531: **Notice.** The indemnified party must provide the indemnifying party with prompt written notice of any third-party claim for which indemnification is sought. Failure to provide prompt notice shall not relieve the indemnifying party of its indemnification obligation except to the extent the indemnifying party is materially prejudiced by the delay.
532: 
533: **Cooperation.** The indemnified party must cooperate with the indemnifying party in the defense of any indemnified claim, including providing access to relevant records, information, and personnel as reasonably requested.
534: 
535: **Control of Defense.** The vendor, as indemnifying party, must have sole control of the defense and settlement of any indemnified claim, including the selection of counsel. TechNova, as indemnified party, has the right to participate in the defense of any indemnified claim with its own counsel at its own expense.
536: 
537: **Settlement Restrictions.** The vendor may not, without TechNova\'s prior written consent, enter into any settlement of an indemnified claim that (a) admits liability or fault on TechNova\'s behalf; (b) imposes any non-monetary obligation on TechNova (including injunctive relief, restrictions on TechNova\'s business activities, or consent decrees); or (c) does not include an unconditional release of TechNova from all liability related to the claim.
538: 
539: **11.4 --- Negotiation Guidance**
540: 
541: If the vendor\'s initial draft limits the IP indemnity to \"direct infringement of registered U.S. patents and copyrights\" or similar narrow language, the negotiating attorney must redline the provision to cover all forms of intellectual property rights and all authorized use, as described in Section 11.1. This expansion is non-negotiable. The negotiating attorney should explain to vendor counsel that the narrow scope commonly found in vendor form agreements does not reflect the breadth of IP risk associated with AI/ML platforms and that TechNova requires comprehensive coverage.
542: 
543: The negotiating attorney should coordinate the IP indemnity scope with the AI-Output Risk Allocation provisions in Section 9 to ensure that there are no gaps in coverage. In particular, the IP indemnity in Section 11 should cover infringement claims related to the vendor\'s Base Model, platform, and pre-existing IP, while the AI-output indemnity in Section 9 should cover claims related to the outputs generated by the vendor\'s model. Together, these two provisions should provide TechNova with comprehensive coverage for all IP-related claims arising from its use of the vendor\'s technology.
544: 
545: **[Section 12 --- Commercial Terms Guidance]{.underline}**
546: 
547: **12.1 --- Fee Structures**
548: 
549: Negotiating attorneys should carefully evaluate all components of the vendor\'s fee structure to ensure they are reasonable relative to market benchmarks and TechNova\'s projected usage. The typical fee structure for an AI/ML vendor engagement includes the following components:
550: 
551: **Annual Platform Fees.** Recurring fees for access to the vendor\'s platform, typically structured as a fixed annual or monthly subscription. Negotiators should benchmark the proposed platform fee against comparable offerings in the market and negotiate volume discounts where TechNova\'s projected usage justifies a lower per-unit cost.
552: 
553: **Implementation Fees.** One-time or project-based fees for the initial deployment, integration, and configuration of the vendor\'s platform for TechNova\'s use. Implementation fees should be structured on a milestone basis to align the vendor\'s financial incentives with successful delivery. A standard milestone structure is fifty percent (50%) of the implementation fee payable at SOW execution and fifty percent (50%) payable at Go-Live (i.e., upon TechNova\'s written acceptance that the platform has been deployed and is operational in TechNova\'s production environment). Alternative milestone structures may be appropriate depending on the complexity of the implementation, but the key principle is that a material portion of the implementation fee should be contingent on successful delivery.
554: 
555: **Usage-Based Overage Charges.** Variable fees for usage in excess of the included usage tiers (e.g., API call volumes, compute hours, token counts). Overage charges should be clearly defined on a per-unit basis, and the per-unit rate should be commercially reasonable and consistent with the vendor\'s published pricing. Negotiators should ensure that the included usage tiers are sized to TechNova\'s projected usage plus a reasonable buffer (typically 15--20% above projected peak usage) to minimize the risk of unexpected overage charges.
556: 
557: **12.2 --- Term and Renewal**
558: 
559: **Initial Term.** Initial terms of three (3) years are standard for strategic AI/ML platform engagements and are generally appropriate for TechNova. A three-year term provides sufficient time for TechNova to realize the full value of the implementation investment while maintaining flexibility to reassess the engagement at the end of the initial term. Shorter initial terms (e.g., one year) may be appropriate for pilot engagements or engagements with unproven vendors, but should be the exception rather than the norm.
560: 
561: **Auto-Renewal.** If the agreement includes an auto-renewal provision, the provision must include a notice period of at least one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the end of the then-current term. This extended notice period is necessary to allow TechNova adequate time to conduct a thorough re-evaluation of the vendor relationship, assess competitive alternatives, and, if appropriate, initiate a procurement process for a replacement vendor. Auto-renewal provisions with shorter notice periods (e.g., 30 or 60 days) create a risk that TechNova will be locked into a renewal before it has had an opportunity to evaluate its options, and should be redlined to provide at least 180 days\' notice.
562: 
563: **12.3 --- Usage Tiers and Overages**
564: 
565: Negotiating attorneys should work with Product Engineering to ensure that the included usage tiers in the agreement are properly sized to TechNova\'s projected usage. The following considerations apply:
566: 
567: **Projected Usage.** Product Engineering should provide a written estimate of TechNova\'s projected monthly and annual usage (e.g., API call volumes, token counts, compute hours) based on current production usage, anticipated growth, and any planned new deployments. The included usage tier in the agreement should be set at a level that accommodates projected usage plus a reasonable buffer.
568: 
569: **Overage Rates.** Overage rates must be commercially reasonable, clearly defined on a per-unit basis (e.g., per thousand API calls, per million tokens, per compute hour), and documented in the agreement or an exhibit thereto. Negotiators should seek to negotiate overage rates that are no higher than the per-unit rate implied by the included usage tier, and should resist vendor proposals for punitive or significantly elevated overage pricing.
570: 
571: **Usage Reporting.** The agreement should require the vendor to provide TechNova with regular usage reports (at least monthly) and real-time usage dashboards or APIs to enable TechNova to monitor its usage against the included tiers and anticipate potential overages.
572: 
573: **[Section 13 --- Document Control and Version History]{.underline}**
574: 
575: This Playbook is maintained jointly by the Legal Department, under the direction of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions (currently Derek Chalmers), and Product Engineering, under the direction of the VP of Product Engineering (currently Priya Anand). All substantive updates to this Playbook require joint review and approval by both maintaining teams prior to publication.
576: 
577: **Current Version:**
578: 
579: > • **Version 3.2 --- March 2025.** Current version. Updates include: (a) revisions to the AI-Output Risk Allocation section (Section 9) to address emerging vendor indemnity requirements and market developments related to generative AI outputs, including the addition of the shared-risk framework as an acceptable fallback position; (b) updates to the Data Processing & Privacy section (Section 4) to reflect regulatory developments under the CPRA and the California Privacy Protection Agency\'s rulemaking activities, including enhanced de-identification standards; and (c) updates to the Liability Framework (Section 5) to clarify the mechanics of the super-cap for IP indemnity and data breach carve-outs, including illustrative dollar-amount examples.
580:

lines.text: > \(c\) **Cessation of Support or End-of-Life.** The vendor ceases product support for the applicable platform or product, announces an end-of-life date for the applicable platform or product, or otherwise discontinues the services provided to TechNova under the agreement.

Release must be automatic upon verification of the trigger event by the escrow agent. The escrow agent must be authorized under the escrow agreement to verify the occurrence of the trigger event based on documentation provided by TechNova (e.g., copies of bankruptcy filings, written breach notices, vendor end-of-life announcements) and to release the escrow materials to TechNova without requiring the vendor\'s consent, approval, or cooperation.
**7.5 --- Negotiation Guidance**

Negotiating attorneys should propose Iron Mountain IPM as the escrow agent in every initial draft. If the vendor insists on an alternative escrow agent, accept only a Tier 1 provider with verifiable AI/ML escrow capabilities. Do not accept a general-purpose escrow agent that lacks specific experience with AI/ML model artifacts, as such agents may not have the technical infrastructure or processes necessary to handle large model files, verify deposit completeness, or support the quarterly update cadence required by this Playbook.

The sixty-day cure period for the material breach release trigger is the TechNova standard. Negotiating attorneys should not agree to extend this period beyond sixty (60) days without the written approval of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions. An extension to ninety (90) days may be acceptable in limited circumstances (e.g., where the nature of the breach reasonably requires additional time to cure), but any extension beyond ninety (90) days is a Red-zone concession.
**[Section 8 --- Insurance Requirements]{.underline}**
**8.1 --- Commercial General Liability (CGL)**

Every AI/ML vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with minimum limits of five million dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence and ten million dollars (\$10,000,000) in the aggregate. This coverage must be maintained throughout the term of the agreement and for a period of at least two (2) years following the expiration or termination of the agreement.

This requirement is standard and non-negotiable. TechNova must be named as an additional insured on the vendor\'s CGL policy. The vendor must provide TechNova with a certificate of insurance evidencing the required coverage prior to the execution of the agreement and annually thereafter during the term.
**8.2 --- Technology Errors & Omissions (Tech E&O)**

**Green (Preferred).** For any AI/ML vendor engagement with a TCV exceeding \$5,000,000, TechNova\'s preferred position is that the vendor maintain technology errors and omissions insurance with a minimum limit of ten million dollars (\$10,000,000) per occurrence. This elevated requirement reflects the heightened risk associated with large-scale AI/ML deployments and the potential magnitude of losses arising from model errors, platform failures, or other technology-related claims.

**Yellow (Acceptable / Minimum).** For all AI/ML vendor engagements (regardless of TCV), the minimum acceptable Tech E&O coverage is five million dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence. This is the absolute floor for Tech E&O coverage.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any Tech E&O coverage below \$5,000,000 per occurrence is a walk-away. Acceptance of a Tech E&O limit below \$5,000,000 requires VP Legal approval with a documented risk assessment.

For engagements with a TCV exceeding \$5,000,000, negotiating attorneys should push firmly for the \$10,000,000 preferred limit. If the vendor\'s current policy limit is \$5,000,000, explore whether the vendor is willing to obtain an endorsement, policy amendment, or increased limits as a condition of the agreement. The cost of increased coverage should be borne by the vendor and should not be passed through to TechNova. If the vendor demonstrates that \$10,000,000 in Tech E&O coverage is not commercially available or is prohibitively expensive, the negotiating attorney should escalate to the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions with a written risk assessment before accepting the \$5,000,000 minimum.
**8.3 --- Umbrella / Excess Liability**

Every AI/ML vendor must maintain umbrella or excess liability insurance with a minimum limit of ten million dollars (\$10,000,000). This coverage must sit excess of the vendor\'s CGL and Tech E&O policies and must provide coverage for claims that exceed the underlying policy limits.
This requirement is standard and non-negotiable.
**8.4 --- Negotiation Guidance**

Insurance requirements should be included in the initial draft of every AI/ML vendor agreement, typically as a schedule or exhibit setting forth the required coverage types and minimum limits. Insurance provisions are generally not traded for concessions in other areas of the negotiation, as they serve a fundamentally different risk-management function than the other commercial and legal terms of the agreement.

If a vendor resists the \$10,000,000 Tech E&O requirement for a high-TCV deal, the negotiating attorney should escalate to the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions with a risk assessment that considers: (a) the TCV and duration of the engagement; (b) the nature of the vendor\'s services and the potential magnitude of technology-related claims; (c) the vendor\'s financial condition and balance sheet strength; and (d) the availability of other contractual protections (e.g., liability caps, indemnification, escrow) that may partially mitigate the risk. Only after this assessment should a decision be made to accept the \$5,000,000 minimum.

Negotiating attorneys should also confirm that the vendor\'s insurance policies do not contain exclusions that would effectively negate coverage for the types of claims most likely to arise in an AI/ML vendor relationship, such as exclusions for AI-generated output claims, data breach claims, or intellectual property infringement claims.
**[Section 9 --- AI-Output Risk Allocation]{.underline}**

This section applies to any AI/ML vendor engagement where the vendor\'s model or platform generates outputs --- including text, predictions, scores, classifications, recommendations, images, code, or any other generated content --- that are used in TechNova\'s customer-facing products or services (e.g., the LendStream platform), or that inform decisions affecting consumers (e.g., credit decisions, risk assessments, customer communications). As AI-generated outputs play an increasingly central role in TechNova\'s product offerings, it is essential that the risk of third-party claims arising from those outputs be appropriately allocated between TechNova and its AI/ML vendors.
**9.2 --- Preferred Position (Green)**
TechNova\'s preferred position is that the vendor provides a full indemnity to TechNova for third-party claims related to AI-generated outputs. Specifically, the vendor\'s indemnity must cover:

> \(a\) **IP Infringement Claims.** Third-party claims alleging that AI-generated outputs infringe, misappropriate, or otherwise violate any intellectual property rights, including patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, and rights of publicity.

> \(b\) **Regulatory and Legal Claims.** Third-party claims alleging that AI-generated outputs violate applicable law, including but not limited to consumer protection statutes, fair lending laws (including the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and the Fair Housing Act), financial services regulations, unfair or deceptive acts or practices (UDAP/UDAAP) prohibitions, and any other federal, state, or local law or regulation applicable to the use of AI-generated outputs in TechNova\'s business.

The indemnity must cover TechNova\'s authorized use of the outputs in accordance with the terms of the agreement and the vendor\'s published documentation and usage guidelines. The vendor may not condition the indemnity on TechNova\'s use of the outputs in a specific manner beyond what is set forth in the agreement and the vendor\'s documentation.
This Green-tier position should be proposed in every initial draft of an AI/ML vendor agreement.
**9.3 --- Acceptable Fallback (Yellow)**
If the vendor will not provide a full output indemnity, TechNova will accept a shared-risk framework structured as follows:

**Vendor First-Dollar Coverage.** The vendor provides first-dollar coverage for defense costs (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) and settlements or judgments arising from third-party claims related to AI-generated outputs, up to the applicable liability cap or super-cap negotiated under Section 5. This means the vendor bears the initial financial exposure for output-related claims, and TechNova is not required to contribute to defense costs or settlements until the vendor\'s coverage tier is exhausted.

**Residual Risk.** TechNova bears the residual risk above the vendor\'s coverage tier. The parties may negotiate the allocation of residual risk above the vendor\'s cap, but the vendor must bear the first-dollar exposure as described above.
**Vendor Obligations.** The shared-risk framework must include the following vendor obligations:

> \(a\) **Cooperation in Defense.** The vendor must cooperate fully with TechNova in the defense of any third-party claim related to AI-generated outputs, including providing access to relevant technical documentation, model architecture information, training data provenance records, and vendor personnel with knowledge of the model\'s design and operation.

> \(b\) **Prompt Remediation.** Upon TechNova\'s notice that an AI-generated output has given rise to a third-party claim or a credible threat of a third-party claim, the vendor must implement prompt remediation measures, which may include retraining the model, adjusting output filters, modifying the inference pipeline, or implementing other technical measures to prevent recurrence of the offending output.
**9.4 --- Carve-Outs**
The vendor\'s AI-output indemnity obligation (whether structured as a full indemnity under Section 9.2 or as a shared-risk framework under Section 9.3) may exclude the following categories of claims:

> \(a\) **Post-Receipt Modification.** Claims caused by TechNova\'s modification of AI-generated outputs after receipt from the vendor\'s platform. For example, if TechNova receives a model prediction from the vendor\'s API and then alters, reformats, or recontextualizes the prediction before presenting it to a consumer, and the claim arises from TechNova\'s modification rather than from the vendor\'s original output, the vendor\'s indemnity obligation does not apply.

> \(b\) **Unauthorized Use.** Claims arising from TechNova\'s use of outputs outside the documented use case or in a manner inconsistent with the vendor\'s published usage guidelines. For example, if the vendor\'s usage guidelines expressly prohibit the use of a particular model for credit decisioning, and TechNova uses the model for credit decisioning notwithstanding that prohibition, the vendor\'s indemnity obligation does not apply to claims arising from that unauthorized use.

No other carve-outs to the vendor\'s AI-output indemnity obligation are acceptable without the express approval of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions. In particular, negotiating attorneys should be alert to vendor proposals that attempt to carve out liability for \"model hallucinations,\" \"accuracy limitations,\" or \"inherent limitations of AI technology.\" Such carve-outs are overbroad and would effectively eliminate the vendor\'s indemnity obligation for the most common categories of AI-output claims.
**9.5 --- Negotiation Guidance**

AI-output risk allocation is a relatively novel provision in AI/ML vendor agreements, and many vendors will not have standard language addressing this issue. Negotiating attorneys should be prepared to propose TechNova\'s preferred position (Section 9.2) in the initial draft and to educate vendor counsel on the rationale for the provision. The key points to communicate are:
> • TechNova is deploying the vendor\'s model in customer-facing products and services, and the outputs generated by the model directly impact TechNova\'s customers.

> • If the vendor\'s model generates an output that infringes a third party\'s intellectual property rights or violates applicable law, TechNova will be the party sued --- and TechNova needs the vendor to stand behind its product.
> • The vendor is best positioned to control the risk associated with its model\'s outputs because the vendor designed, trained, and maintains the model.

If the vendor has not previously addressed AI-output risk allocation in its standard terms, the shared-risk framework described in Section 9.3 is an acceptable landing zone and should be presented as a reasonable compromise. Emphasize that the shared-risk framework limits the vendor\'s exposure to the applicable liability cap or super-cap, which already constrains the vendor\'s total financial exposure.

Negotiating attorneys should coordinate with Product Engineering to document the specific use cases and output types that will be covered by the AI-output indemnity. A clear and specific description of \"authorized use\" will strengthen TechNova\'s position in any future claim and will provide the vendor with reasonable certainty about the scope of its obligation.

Any vendor that categorically refuses both the full indemnity (Section 9.2) and the shared-risk framework (Section 9.3) --- that is, any vendor that takes the position that it has no responsibility whatsoever for claims arising from its model\'s outputs --- should be flagged for escalation to the VP Legal. Categorical refusal to accept any form of AI-output risk allocation is a Red-zone position.
**[Section 10 --- Governing Law & Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**
**10.1 --- Governing Law**

**Green (Preferred / Strong Preference).** TechNova\'s strong preference is that all AI/ML vendor agreements be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Delaware law provides a well-developed, predictable, and commercially sophisticated body of contract law, and TechNova\'s corporate governance structure is organized under Delaware law. This preference should be reflected in every initial draft.
**Yellow (Acceptable Alternatives).** If the vendor will not agree to Delaware governing law, TechNova will accept either of the following alternatives:

> • **New York law**, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. New York has a similarly well-developed body of commercial contract law and is widely accepted as a governing law choice for technology transactions.

> • **Texas law**, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. TechNova\'s principal offices are located in Austin, Texas, and Texas law is an appropriate alternative governing law choice for engagements with Texas-based vendors or where the services will be primarily performed in Texas.
Either of these alternatives falls within the Yellow zone and may be accepted by the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions without further escalation.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any governing law other than Delaware, New York, or Texas is a walk-away absent VP Legal approval. This includes, without limitation, the vendor\'s home-state law (unless the vendor is domiciled in Delaware, New York, or Texas), foreign law, or any other jurisdiction that does not provide the predictability and sophistication of Delaware, New York, or Texas commercial contract law.
**10.2 --- Forum / Dispute Resolution**

**Preferred.** TechNova\'s preferred dispute resolution forum is exclusive jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery, or, if the Court of Chancery declines jurisdiction (e.g., because the dispute involves a claim for money damages that is not ancillary to equitable relief), the United States District Court for the District of Delaware. The Delaware Court of Chancery provides expedited proceedings, experienced judges with expertise in commercial disputes, and well-developed procedural rules for complex business litigation.

**Acceptable Alternative.** If the vendor will not agree to a Delaware forum, TechNova will accept exclusive jurisdiction in the federal or state courts located in one of the following jurisdictions, consistent with the governing law selected:
> • **New York:** The United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, or the Commercial Division of the New York Supreme Court, New York County.
> • **Texas:** The United States District Court for the Western District of Texas, Austin Division, or the state courts of Travis County, Texas.

**Avoid: Mandatory Binding Arbitration.** TechNova\'s strong preference is to avoid mandatory binding arbitration for any dispute, and particularly for disputes with an amount in controversy exceeding \$1,000,000. Mandatory arbitration limits TechNova\'s discovery rights, eliminates the right to appeal, and may result in an unreasoned award that does not provide adequate guidance for the parties\' ongoing relationship.
If the vendor insists on mandatory arbitration, the negotiating attorney should pursue the following alternatives in order of preference:

> \(a\) **Litigation Carve-Out.** Negotiate a carve-out providing that disputes with an amount in controversy exceeding \$1,000,000 shall be resolved by litigation in the agreed forum (Delaware, New York, or Texas courts), with arbitration applicable only to disputes below the \$1,000,000 threshold.

> \(b\) **Enhanced Arbitration.** If a litigation carve-out is not achievable, negotiate enhanced arbitration terms that provide TechNova with protections approximating those available in litigation, including at minimum: (i) a three-arbitrator panel; (ii) arbitration administered under the American Arbitration Association (\"AAA\") Commercial Rules; (iii) full discovery rights, including document production and depositions; and (iv) a reasoned written award setting forth the arbitrators\' findings of fact and conclusions of law.
**10.3 --- Negotiation Guidance**

Open with Delaware law and a Delaware forum in every initial draft. If the vendor proposes its home-state law or mandatory arbitration, counter with Delaware and flag the issue for the negotiating team.

Do not concede to mandatory arbitration for high-value disputes without first exploring the litigation carve-out described in Section 10.2(a). If arbitration is ultimately unavoidable, insist on the enhanced arbitration terms described in Section 10.2(b). Under no circumstances should TechNova agree to arbitration before a single arbitrator, arbitration without discovery rights, or arbitration resulting in an unreasoned award.

If the vendor is domiciled in a jurisdiction other than Delaware, New York, or Texas, the vendor will likely push for its home-state law and forum. In such cases, the negotiating attorney should explain TechNova\'s strong preference for a neutral, commercially sophisticated jurisdiction and propose Delaware as a true neutral forum. If the vendor resists Delaware, explore New York or Texas as alternatives. If the vendor will not agree to any of the three approved jurisdictions, escalate to the VP Legal before accepting an alternative.
**[Section 11 --- Indemnification]{.underline}**
**11.1 --- Scope of IP Indemnity**

**Green (Preferred) / Minimum (Non-Negotiable).** The vendor\'s intellectual property indemnity must cover all forms of intellectual property rights, without limitation. Specifically, the indemnity must cover claims alleging infringement, misappropriation, or violation of:

> \(a\) **Patents** --- including utility patents, design patents, and provisional patent rights, whether registered or unregistered, and whether issued in the United States or in any foreign jurisdiction.
> \(b\) **Copyrights** --- including rights in original works of authorship, derivative works, compilations, and databases, whether registered or unregistered.

> \(c\) **Trade Secrets** --- including rights in proprietary algorithms, methodologies, techniques, processes, and know-how, whether or not the information qualifies as a \"trade secret\" under the Defend Trade Secrets Act or applicable state uniform trade secrets acts.
> \(d\) **Trademarks** --- including rights in registered and unregistered trademarks, service marks, trade names, and trade dress.

> \(e\) **Rights of Publicity and Moral Rights** --- to the extent applicable under the law of any relevant jurisdiction, including claims alleging unauthorized use of a person\'s name, likeness, or identity in AI-generated outputs.

The indemnity must not be limited to registered United States patents and copyrights. Many vendor form agreements contain IP indemnity provisions that are narrowly scoped to cover only \"infringement of a valid, issued U.S. patent or registered U.S. copyright.\" This narrow scope is insufficient for TechNova\'s purposes, as it would leave TechNova without indemnification coverage for trade secret misappropriation claims (which are increasingly common in the AI/ML space), trademark infringement claims, foreign IP claims, and claims based on unregistered copyrights. Any vendor draft that narrows the indemnity to only registered U.S. patents and copyrights must be revised to cover all intellectual property rights as described above.

The indemnity must cover TechNova\'s authorized use of the vendor\'s platform, models, and outputs in accordance with the agreement. The indemnity should not be conditioned on TechNova\'s use of the vendor\'s platform in an unmodified form or on TechNova\'s exclusive use of the vendor\'s recommended configuration, provided that TechNova\'s use is within the scope of the authorized use described in the agreement.
**11.2 --- Standard Indemnity Obligations**

**Vendor\'s Indemnification of TechNova.** The vendor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless TechNova and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all third-party claims, losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or relating to:

> \(a\) Infringement or misappropriation of any intellectual property right by the vendor\'s platform, models, outputs, or any component thereof, when used by TechNova as authorized under the agreement.

> \(b\) The vendor\'s breach of its data processing and privacy obligations as set forth in the agreement and the applicable DPA (see Section 4), including any breach resulting in unauthorized access to, disclosure of, or loss of TechNova customer data.

> \(c\) The vendor\'s violation of applicable law in the performance of the agreement, including violations of consumer protection, fair lending, financial services, and data privacy laws and regulations.

**TechNova\'s Indemnification of Vendor.** TechNova will indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the vendor and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all third-party claims, losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or relating to:
> \(a\) TechNova\'s breach of the agreement, including any breach of TechNova\'s representations, warranties, or covenants.

> \(b\) TechNova\'s use of the vendor\'s platform or outputs in a manner that is not authorized by the agreement or that is inconsistent with the vendor\'s published documentation and usage guidelines.
**11.3 --- Indemnity Procedures**
The agreement must include standard indemnification procedures, including the following:

**Notice.** The indemnified party must provide the indemnifying party with prompt written notice of any third-party claim for which indemnification is sought. Failure to provide prompt notice shall not relieve the indemnifying party of its indemnification obligation except to the extent the indemnifying party is materially prejudiced by the delay.

**Cooperation.** The indemnified party must cooperate with the indemnifying party in the defense of any indemnified claim, including providing access to relevant records, information, and personnel as reasonably requested.

**Control of Defense.** The vendor, as indemnifying party, must have sole control of the defense and settlement of any indemnified claim, including the selection of counsel. TechNova, as indemnified party, has the right to participate in the defense of any indemnified claim with its own counsel at its own expense.

**Settlement Restrictions.** The vendor may not, without TechNova\'s prior written consent, enter into any settlement of an indemnified claim that (a) admits liability or fault on TechNova\'s behalf; (b) imposes any non-monetary obligation on TechNova (including injunctive relief, restrictions on TechNova\'s business activities, or consent decrees); or (c) does not include an unconditional release of TechNova from all liability related to the claim.
**11.4 --- Negotiation Guidance**

If the vendor\'s initial draft limits the IP indemnity to \"direct infringement of registered U.S. patents and copyrights\" or similar narrow language, the negotiating attorney must redline the provision to cover all forms of intellectual property rights and all authorized use, as described in Section 11.1. This expansion is non-negotiable. The negotiating attorney should explain to vendor counsel that the narrow scope commonly found in vendor form agreements does not reflect the breadth of IP risk associated with AI/ML platforms and that TechNova requires comprehensive coverage.

The negotiating attorney should coordinate the IP indemnity scope with the AI-Output Risk Allocation provisions in Section 9 to ensure that there are no gaps in coverage. In particular, the IP indemnity in Section 11 should cover infringement claims related to the vendor\'s Base Model, platform, and pre-existing IP, while the AI-output indemnity in Section 9 should cover claims related to the outputs generated by the vendor\'s model. Together, these two provisions should provide TechNova with comprehensive coverage for all IP-related claims arising from its use of the vendor\'s technology.
**[Section 12 --- Commercial Terms Guidance]{.underline}**
**12.1 --- Fee Structures**

Negotiating attorneys should carefully evaluate all components of the vendor\'s fee structure to ensure they are reasonable relative to market benchmarks and TechNova\'s projected usage. The typical fee structure for an AI/ML vendor engagement includes the following components:

**Annual Platform Fees.** Recurring fees for access to the vendor\'s platform, typically structured as a fixed annual or monthly subscription. Negotiators should benchmark the proposed platform fee against comparable offerings in the market and negotiate volume discounts where TechNova\'s projected usage justifies a lower per-unit cost.

**Implementation Fees.** One-time or project-based fees for the initial deployment, integration, and configuration of the vendor\'s platform for TechNova\'s use. Implementation fees should be structured on a milestone basis to align the vendor\'s financial incentives with successful delivery. A standard milestone structure is fifty percent (50%) of the implementation fee payable at SOW execution and fifty percent (50%) payable at Go-Live (i.e., upon TechNova\'s written acceptance that the platform has been deployed and is operational in TechNova\'s production environment). Alternative milestone structures may be appropriate depending on the complexity of the implementation, but the key principle is that a material portion of the implementation fee should be contingent on successful delivery.

**Usage-Based Overage Charges.** Variable fees for usage in excess of the included usage tiers (e.g., API call volumes, compute hours, token counts). Overage charges should be clearly defined on a per-unit basis, and the per-unit rate should be commercially reasonable and consistent with the vendor\'s published pricing. Negotiators should ensure that the included usage tiers are sized to TechNova\'s projected usage plus a reasonable buffer (typically 15--20% above projected peak usage) to minimize the risk of unexpected overage charges.
**12.2 --- Term and Renewal**

**Initial Term.** Initial terms of three (3) years are standard for strategic AI/ML platform engagements and are generally appropriate for TechNova. A three-year term provides sufficient time for TechNova to realize the full value of the implementation investment while maintaining flexibility to reassess the engagement at the end of the initial term. Shorter initial terms (e.g., one year) may be appropriate for pilot engagements or engagements with unproven vendors, but should be the exception rather than the norm.

**Auto-Renewal.** If the agreement includes an auto-renewal provision, the provision must include a notice period of at least one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the end of the then-current term. This extended notice period is necessary to allow TechNova adequate time to conduct a thorough re-evaluation of the vendor relationship, assess competitive alternatives, and, if appropriate, initiate a procurement process for a replacement vendor. Auto-renewal provisions with shorter notice periods (e.g., 30 or 60 days) create a risk that TechNova will be locked into a renewal before it has had an opportunity to evaluate its options, and should be redlined to provide at least 180 days\' notice.
**12.3 --- Usage Tiers and Overages**

Negotiating attorneys should work with Product Engineering to ensure that the included usage tiers in the agreement are properly sized to TechNova\'s projected usage. The following considerations apply:

**Projected Usage.** Product Engineering should provide a written estimate of TechNova\'s projected monthly and annual usage (e.g., API call volumes, token counts, compute hours) based on current production usage, anticipated growth, and any planned new deployments. The included usage tier in the agreement should be set at a level that accommodates projected usage plus a reasonable buffer.

**Overage Rates.** Overage rates must be commercially reasonable, clearly defined on a per-unit basis (e.g., per thousand API calls, per million tokens, per compute hour), and documented in the agreement or an exhibit thereto. Negotiators should seek to negotiate overage rates that are no higher than the per-unit rate implied by the included usage tier, and should resist vendor proposals for punitive or significantly elevated overage pricing.

**Usage Reporting.** The agreement should require the vendor to provide TechNova with regular usage reports (at least monthly) and real-time usage dashboards or APIs to enable TechNova to monitor its usage against the included tiers and anticipate potential overages.
**[Section 13 --- Document Control and Version History]{.underline}**

This Playbook is maintained jointly by the Legal Department, under the direction of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions (currently Derek Chalmers), and Product Engineering, under the direction of the VP of Product Engineering (currently Priya Anand). All substantive updates to this Playbook require joint review and approval by both maintaining teams prior to publication.
**Current Version:**

> • **Version 3.2 --- March 2025.** Current version. Updates include: (a) revisions to the AI-Output Risk Allocation section (Section 9) to address emerging vendor indemnity requirements and market developments related to generative AI outputs, including the addition of the shared-risk framework as an acceptable fallback position; (b) updates to the Data Processing & Privacy section (Section 4) to reflect regulatory developments under the CPRA and the California Privacy Protection Agency\'s rulemaking activities, including enhanced de-identification standards; and (c) updates to the Liability Framework (Section 5) to clarify the mechanics of the super-cap for IP indemnity and data breach carve-outs, including illustrative dollar-amount examples.
**Prior Versions:**

> • **Version 3.1 --- September 2024.** Added escrow requirements for AI/ML model artifacts (Section 7); updated insurance requirements for Tech E&O coverage (Section 8); added Appendix B (Approved Escrow Agents).

> • **Version 3.0 --- March 2024.** Major revision. Restructured the Playbook to adopt the three-tier classification framework (Green/Yellow/Red); added the Decision Matrix and Escalation Procedures (Section 2); expanded IP Ownership & Licensing provisions (Section 3); added AI-Output Risk Allocation section (Section 9, initial version).
> • **Version 2.0 --- September 2023.** Added Data Processing & Privacy section (Section 4) to address CCPA/CPRA compliance; updated SLA provisions (Section 6).
> • **Version 1.0 --- March 2023.** Initial version.

**Next Scheduled Review:** September 2025. The maintaining teams will conduct a comprehensive review of all sections to incorporate any developments in AI/ML vendor market practices, regulatory requirements, and TechNova\'s evolving business needs.
**Distribution:** This Playbook is classified as CONFIDENTIAL --- Internal Use Only. It is distributed to the following personnel and teams:
> • Legal Department (all attorneys and legal professionals involved in AI/ML vendor transactions)
> • Product Engineering leadership (VP of Product Engineering and direct reports)
> • Procurement Department (all procurement professionals involved in AI/ML vendor sourcing)
> • Outside counsel engaged on AI/ML vendor transactions (subject to applicable confidentiality obligations and engagement letters)
This Playbook may not be distributed to any AI/ML vendor, vendor counsel, or other external party without the prior written approval of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions.
**[Appendix A --- Term-by-Term Decision Matrix (Quick Reference)]{.underline}**

The following table is provided as a quick-reference summary of the Green, Yellow, and Red positions for each major term addressed in this Playbook. Negotiating attorneys should consult the referenced sections for detailed guidance, negotiation strategy, and illustrative examples.
