**[Appendix B --- Approved Escrow Agents]{.underline}**
**Tier 1 --- Preferred**
**Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc.**

Iron Mountain IPM is TechNova\'s preferred escrow agent for all AI/ML vendor engagements requiring escrow deposits. Iron Mountain IPM has demonstrated experience in technology escrow and has developed specific capabilities for AI/ML model artifact escrow, including secure handling of large binary model weight files, structured deposit verification processes, and support for quarterly deposit update schedules. Iron Mountain IPM should be proposed as the escrow agent in every initial draft of an AI/ML vendor agreement that includes an escrow requirement.
**Tier 1 --- Acceptable Alternatives**

**NCC Group plc.** NCC Group is an acceptable Tier 1 alternative escrow agent. NCC Group has a well-established technology escrow practice and has expanded its capabilities to include AI/ML model artifact deposits. NCC Group may be accepted as the escrow agent where the vendor has a pre-existing escrow relationship with NCC Group or where other circumstances make NCC Group a practical alternative.

**Other Providers.** Other technology escrow providers may be accepted as Tier 1 alternatives on a case-by-case basis, subject to the written approval of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions. Approval will be based on the following selection criteria:

> • **AI/ML Experience.** The provider must have demonstrated experience in receiving, storing, and managing AI/ML model deposits, including large binary weight files, training configuration files, and pipeline artifacts.

> • **SOC 2 Type II Certification.** The provider must hold a current SOC 2 Type II certification, evidencing that its controls over security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy have been independently audited and found to be operating effectively.

> • **Quarterly Update Support.** The provider must have the operational capability to support quarterly deposit updates (or more frequent updates upon material model version changes), including secure upload mechanisms and verification processes for each update.
> • **Standard Three-Party Agreement.** The provider must offer a standard three-party escrow agreement that is consistent with market practice and acceptable to TechNova\'s Legal Department.
Any proposed escrow agent that does not meet these criteria should not be accepted without escalation to the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions.
**[Appendix C --- Required DPA Provisions Checklist]{.underline}**

The following checklist is provided for use by negotiating attorneys to confirm that every Data Processing Agreement (DPA) attached to or incorporated into an AI/ML vendor agreement includes the minimum required provisions. This checklist should be completed for each agreement and retained in the deal file.
**Negotiating Attorney:** **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

**No.**           **Required Provision**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 **Included (Y/N)**   **Comments**

1                 **CCPA Service-Provider Certification.** DPA includes a certification by the vendor that it understands and will comply with the restrictions applicable to service providers under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), including restrictions on retention, use, and disclosure of personal information.

2                 **GLBA Compliance Obligations.** DPA includes the vendor\'s agreement to comply with GLBA requirements and to maintain appropriate safeguards for NPPI in accordance with the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) and any other applicable GLBA implementing regulations.

3                 **Specification of Business Purpose.** DPA specifies the business purpose(s) for which the vendor is authorized to process TechNova customer data, with sufficient specificity to enable compliance verification.

4                 **Prohibition on Sale or Sharing.** DPA includes an express prohibition on the vendor\'s sale or sharing (as defined in the CCPA/CPRA) of TechNova customer data, including any personal information derived from or based on TechNova customer data.

5                 **Prohibition on Third-Party Model Training.** DPA includes an express prohibition on the vendor\'s use of TechNova customer data (including derivatives) for training, improving, or fine-tuning any models or algorithms for the benefit of third parties or the vendor\'s general-purpose product offerings.

6                 **72-Hour Data Breach Notification.** DPA requires the vendor to notify TechNova in writing within 72 hours of the vendor\'s discovery of any actual or reasonably suspected data breach, security incident, or unauthorized access, acquisition, use, or disclosure of TechNova customer data.

7                 **Sub-Processor Restrictions.** DPA prohibits the vendor from engaging any sub-processor to process TechNova customer data without TechNova\'s prior written consent, and requires the vendor to provide a current sub-processor list and at least 30 days\' advance notice of proposed sub-processor changes.

8                 **Data Return and Deletion.** DPA requires the vendor, upon termination or expiration of the agreement, to return or securely delete all TechNova customer data in its possession, including all copies, backups, and derivatives, and to provide written certification of deletion upon TechNova\'s request.

9                 **Audit Rights.** DPA grants TechNova the right to audit the vendor\'s compliance with the DPA and applicable data processing and privacy obligations at least annually, upon at least 30 days\' prior written notice, at TechNova\'s expense (unless the audit reveals a material non-compliance, in which case the vendor bears the cost of the audit).

10                **De-Identification Requirements.** If the vendor has been granted any right to use de-identified or aggregated data, the DPA requires that de-identification meet the CCPA statutory standard (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m)) and that compliance be verified by an independent third-party auditor approved by TechNova prior to any use of the de-identified data.

After that, I'll use python-docx to load it, apply necessary modifications at the paragraph level, and ensure I retain formatting.

**Creating a new docx with redlines**

I’m considering creating a new docx by converting the clean base to text, although preserving the whole formatting isn't as critical. I need actual redlines to show changes. 

To achieve this, I can use XML to find all paragraphs and text tokens. I think I could write a function to replace exact target strings while preserving styles. My plan is to search through the clean base text, ensuring I replace only those specific strings without disrupting any formatting. I'll use `python-docx` to recursively process all paragraphs and tables for replacements.

**Reconstructing paragraphs with formatting**

I’m thinking about creating a new set of runs from paragraph text segmentation by deleting target w:del entries and inserting w:ins with w:r/w:t. The idea is to remove all original runs in the paragraph and recreate them with a single run; formatting should be preserved, but there's no need to keep the bold or underline. 

For headings, they might lose their bold formatting, but that could be okay if it's minimal. Given the large document size, I should only reconstruct the touched paragraphs while keeping untouched formatting intact. I also need to inspect the existing runs to see if the target text is in one run.

I’m thinking about how to track changes in a Word document using the Word package. I should use w:ins and w:del for insertions and deletions and set the revision author and date accordingly. It looks like I'll need to include document settings for tracking revisions, such as adding w:trackRevisions. 192: Section 9.1 — Uptime
193: Vendor shall  maintain Platform availability of at least  ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the "Uptime SLA"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
194: Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100
195: For purposes of the Uptime SLA, "Downtime" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor's monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in  this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer's systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer's acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer's access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).
196: Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours' advance written notice to Customer's designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
197: Section 9.2 — Latency
198: Vendor shall  maintain API response latency at or below  four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤  400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor's internal monitoring systems at the Platform's API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor's receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor's transmission of the corresponding API response.
199: Section 9.3 — Model Accuracy
200: Vendor shall  maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above  zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset  established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer's production document processing workloads.
201: During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.
202: Section 9.4 — Service Credits
203: In the event Vendor fails to meet the  Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any  applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a "Service Credit"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the  SLA failure occurred.
204:  Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer's next invoice(s) under this Agreement  . If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed  thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Service Credits are not Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5.

346: 1. Scope of Implementation Services
347: Vendor shall perform the following Implementation Services in connection with the deployment and configuration of the Platform for Customer's use with LendStream:
348: (a) Environment Provisioning. Vendor shall provision and configure Customer's dedicated Platform environment, including allocation of compute resources, storage, and network infrastructure necessary to support Customer's anticipated workloads. 380: The following service level targets shall apply during the Term:
382: Stabilization Period: During the ninety (90)-day Stabilization Period following Go-Live, the Model Accuracy (F1) target shall be ≥ 0.90 (informational only; no Service Credits shall accrue for accuracy during the Stabilization Period).
383: 2. Scheduled Maintenance
384: Vendor may schedule maintenance windows of up to four (4) hours per calendar month for the purpose of performing routine maintenance, upgrades, patches, and other operational activities on the Platform. Scheduled maintenance shall not be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA, provided that the following conditions are met:
385: (a) Vendor provides Customer with at least  seventy-two (72) hours' prior written notice (via email to Customer's designated technical contact) of the scheduled maintenance window, specifying the date, start time, estimated duration, and nature of the maintenance activity;
386: (b) Scheduled maintenance windows are scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and  5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable; and
387: (c) The total duration of scheduled maintenance does not exceed four (4) hours in any single calendar month.
388: Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite  seventy-two (72) hours' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
389: 3. Force Majeure Exclusion
390: Downtime resulting from Force Majeure Events, as defined in Section 14.5 of the Agreement, shall be excluded from the calculation of Platform availability for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
392: 4. Service Credit Schedule — Uptime Failures
393: In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA in any calendar month, Customer shall be entitled to a Service Credit calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment ($200,000) for the affected calendar month, in accordance with the following tiered schedule:
395: | Below 99.50% | 30% ($60,000) |
396: [ADDED: ### 4A. Service Credit Schedule — Latency Failures
397: If p95 latency exceeds 400 ms for any calendar month, an additional Service Credit of 5% of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment ($10,000) shall apply, subject to the overall monthly cap set forth in Section 5(c).]
398: [ADDED: ### 4B. Service Credit Schedule — Accuracy Failures

400: 5. Service Credit Terms and Conditions
401: (a) Request Requirement. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor's support team within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the  SLA failure occurred. The request must identify the specific dates and times of the  SLA failure and reference the applicable monthly service report. Vendor shall validate the claim against its monitoring data and notify Customer of the approved Service Credit amount within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the request.
402: (b) Application of Credits. Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against the next invoice(s) issued to Customer under the Agreement.  If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days.
403: (c) Maximum Credits. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. 
404: (d) ** Remedies.** Service Credits  are not Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5 of the Agreement.

from lxml import etree
import re
src='documents/technova-ai-vendor-agreement-draft-2-redline.docx'; out='clean-accepted.docx'
W='http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main'; ns={'w':W}; q=lambda t:f'{{{W}}}{t}'
def accept(root):
for ins in list(root.xpath('.//w:ins',namespaces=ns)):
par=ins.getparent(); i=par.index(ins)
for ch in list(ins): par.insert(i,ch); i+=1
par.remove(ins)
for de in list(root.xpath('.//w:del',namespaces=ns)): de.getparent().remove(de)
return root
def clean(s):
old=s
for _ in range(10):
s=re.sub(r'\\?\[DELETED:\s*(.*?)\\?\]', '', s, flags=re.S)
s=re.sub(r'\\?\[ADDED:\s*(.*?)\\?\]', lambda m:m.group(1), s, flags=re.S)
if s==old: break
old=s
return s
with ZipFile(src) as z: files={n:z.read(n) for n in z.namelist()}
r=etree.fromstring(files['word/document.xml']); accept(r)
for p in r.xpath('.//w:p',namespaces=ns):
texts=p.xpath('.//w:t/text()',namespaces=ns)
s=''.join(texts)
c=clean(s)
if c!=s:
ppr=p.find(q('pPr')); rpr=None
for rr in p.xpath('.//w:r',namespaces=ns):
x=rr.find(q('rPr'))
if x is not None: rpr=etree.fromstring(etree.tostring(x)); break
for ch in list(p):
if ch is not ppr: p.remove(ch)
if c:
rr=etree.SubElement(p,q('r'))
if rpr is not None: rr.append(rpr)
tt=etree.SubElement(rr,q('t')); tt.set('{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space','preserve'); tt.text=c
files['word/document.xml']=etree.tostring(r,xml_declaration=True,encoding='UTF-8',standalone='yes')
with ZipFile(out,'w',ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
for n,b in files.items(): z.writestr(n,b)
print(out)

def accept(root):

for ch in list(ins): par.insert(i,ch); i+=1
par.remove(ins)

return root

mode=None
starts={"[DELETED:":"deleted", "\\[DELETED:":"deleted", "[ADDED:":"added", "\\[ADDED:":"added"}
for node in root.xpath('.//w:t',namespaces=ns):
s=node.text or ''; out=''; i=0
while i < len(s):
if mode is None:
hits=[(s.find(tok,i),tok) for tok in starts if s.find(tok,i)>=0]
if hits:
pos,tok=min(hits); out+=s[i:pos]; mode=starts[tok]; i=pos+len(tok); continue
out+=s[i:]; break
else:
# closing marker may be escaped or plain; use first occurrence
poss=[x for x in (s.find('\\]',i),s.find(']',i)) if x>=0]

pos=min(poss);
if mode=='added': out+=s[i:pos]
mode=None; i=pos+(2 if s.startswith('\\]',pos) else 1); continue

break
node.text=out

# --- XML helpers ---
def ptext(p):
    vals=[]
    for node in p.xpath('.//w:t',namespaces=ns): vals.append(node.text or '')
    return ''.join(vals)

def first_rpr(p):
    for r in p.xpath('.//w:r',namespaces=ns):
        x=r.find(q('rPr'))
        if x is not None: return deepcopy(x)
    return None

def make_run(text, rpr=None, deleted=False):
    r=etree.Element(q('r'))
    if rpr is not None: r.append(deepcopy(rpr))
    t=etree.SubElement(r,q('delText' if deleted else 't'))
    t.set('{%s}space'%XML,'preserve'); t.text=text
    return r

def make_revision(text, deleted=False):
    tag='del' if deleted else 'ins'
    el=etree.Element(q(tag),{q('id'):str(REV),q('author'):AUTH,q('date'):DATE})
    el.append(make_run(text, deleted=deleted))
    return el

    s=ptext(p)
    if old not in s: return False
    rpr=first_rpr(p); pos=s.index(old)
    before, after=s[:pos], s[pos+len(old):]
    ppr=p.find(q('pPr'))
    for ch in list(p):
        if ch is not ppr: p.remove(ch)
    for txt in (before,):
        if txt: p.append(make_run(txt,rpr))
    p.append(make_revision(old,deleted=True))
    p.append(make_revision(new,deleted=False))
    if after: p.append(make_run(after,rpr))
    return True

def replace_full(p, new):
    return replace_p(p,ptext(p),new)

    p.addnext(np)

    for p in paras():

        if pred(t): return p
    return None

I'll aim for a landscape layout with 7 columns for a wider table. The final document needs to include 14 issues and exact statuses in a specific format. I'll also add footnotes, source basis lists, and validate commercial terms to meet the requirements thoroughly.

**Reviewing caution flags**

I’m compiling a list of caution flags that need to be included. For latency, we have yellow at 450, but the product prefers it to be ≤400. Tech E&O is also yellow with a 5M acceptance versus a preferred 10M. There are specifics regarding accuracy and SLA credits that need to be addressed. IP indemnity is non-negotiable, and I must remember to include detailed commercial terms and financial projections like the TCV for clarity.

However, it’s worth noting that not all open items need to be marked in red. I want to make this clear and effective for anyone reading the document, so it’s essential to establish a consistent color-coding system that everyone can easily understand. That way, it enhances readability!

from docx import Document

out='output/updated-issues-list.docx'

def set_cell_text(cell, text, bold=False, color=None, size=8.5):

    p=cell.paragraphs[0]
    p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)

    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(*color)
    cell.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=60, start=80, bottom=60, end=80):
    tc=cell._tc; tcPr=tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); tcMar=tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None: tcMar=OxmlElement('w:tcMar'); tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m,v in [('top',top),('start',start),('bottom',bottom),('end',end)]:
        node=tcMar.find(qn('w:'+m))
        if node is None: node=OxmlElement('w:'+m); tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'),str(v)); node.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa')

def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr=row._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); rep=OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); rep.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(rep)

def set_col_widths(table, widths):

p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
r=p.add_run('TECHNOVA SOLUTIONS, INC.'); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(9); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(31,78,121)
p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Title'); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER; p.add_run('Updated Negotiation Issues List')

p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(3)
r=p.add_run('Purpose. '); r.bold=True
p.add_run('This list tracks each material negotiation point after applying the Draft 3 instructions. “Resolved” means the point is sufficiently agreed for Draft 3; “Partially Resolved” means the core direction is aligned but a qualification, business confirmation, or drafting detail remains; “Open” means Meridian has not agreed or the point remains expressly reserved.')

# status legend
p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(3)
r=p.add_run('Caution legend: '); r.bold=True
for label,color in [('Yellow / fallback',(156,101,0)),('Red / escalation or walk-away',(192,0,0)),('Product caution',(31,78,121))]:
    rr=p.add_run(label+'  '); rr.bold=True; rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(*color)

issues=[
(1,'Uptime SLA (99.95% monthly)','Resolved','Draft 3 carries 99.95% monthly uptime with scheduled-maintenance exclusions (72-hour notice; four-hour monthly limit) and Force Majeure exclusions.','Green / floor satisfied','No fallback needed; retain the agreed exclusions and measurement language.'),
(2,'Latency (p95 ≤450 ms accepted; product prefers ≤400 ms)','Partially Resolved','Draft 3 proposes p95 ≤450 ms at the API gateway, consistent with Meridian’s May 6 offer and the instruction email.','YELLOW CAUTION — Product Engineering / Priya still prefers sub-400 ms for LendStream real-time decisioning.','Revisit at the week-of-May-19 joint call. (3,'Accuracy / F1 score (0.92 ramp to 0.94)','Open','Draft 3 proposes F1 ≥0.92 during the 90-day stabilization period (Oct. 1–Dec. 31, 2025) and F1 ≥0.94 beginning Jan. 1, 2026.','Yellow floor is F1 ≥0.92; below 0.92 is Red / walk-away. (4,'SLA credits (20% cap / $40,000 per month)','Open','Draft 3 proposes an aggregate monthly cap of 20% of the $200,000 monthly platform fee ($40,000), with automatic application or simple notice/validation mechanics.','Yellow floor / caution: 20% is the Playbook minimum; TechNova’s preferred position is 30%.','Do not accept below 20% without VP Legal approval. (6,'Liability cap ($3.6M compromise)','Open','Draft 3 proposes a general cap of 1.5× annual platform fees = $3,600,000.','Yellow compromise / Playbook floor. (7,'Super-cap ($7.2M for IP indemnity and data breach)','Partially Resolved','Draft 3 converts the accepted concept into a 3× annual-fee super-cap of $7,200,000 for IP indemnity and data-breach liability. Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain uncapped.','Yellow minimum accepted; caution that this is not TechNova’s preferred uncapped treatment for IP/data breach.','Fallback is the 3× super-cap; no cap may apply to willful misconduct or gross negligence.'),
(8,'Data processing / CCPA service-provider and de-identified data','Partially Resolved','Draft 3 includes CCPA service-provider certification under Cal. Civ. Code §1798.140(ag), GLBA/CCPA-CPRA references, 72-hour notice from awareness, prior written consent for sub-processors, and a specific de-identification condition.','Mandatory / non-negotiable: no independent-controller treatment; de-identification requires the statutory CCPA standard plus independent verification by a TechNova-approved assessor before use.','No concession on mandatory DPA requirements. If Meridian will not accept verified de-identification, remove the model-improvement use right and escalate any proposed deviation.'),
(9,'AI-output indemnity (new provision)','Open','Draft 3 inserts full vendor indemnity for third-party claims that AI-generated outputs infringe IP rights or violate applicable law, subject only to Customer modification and out-of-scope use carve-outs.','Green primary; novel-risk caution. (10,'IP indemnity scope (all IP rights / authorized use)','Open','Draft 3 broadens the existing provision to all IP rights, including patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, publicity/moral rights, database rights, and analogous foreign-law rights, for authorized use.','Non-negotiable scope; narrow registered-U.S.-patent/copyright-only language is Red.','No Yellow concession on scope. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).
